## Spoiler Warning
I just got back from seeing Christopher Nolan's adaptation of _The Odyssey_ , and I have a lot to say about it.
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This review contains spoilers. If you have not seen the movie, close this article, go watch it, and come back. I do not want to hear anybody complaining that I spoiled it for them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/394a3771-f79b-4d33-aedd-02005e88c83b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I would also recommend learning the basic story of _The Odyssey_ before watching the movie. You do not need to read Homer's entire epic, but a quick overview will make the characters, mythology, and structure much easier to follow.
I am going to do three things here:
**First** , explain the basic story.
**Second** , talk about the political backlash surrounding the movie.
**Finally** , explain why I think Nolan's _The Odyssey_ is a 9 out of 10 epic about war, masculinity, addiction, leadership, and what happens when the norms holding a society together begin to collapse.
* * *
## What Is _The Odyssey_?
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_The Odyssey_ is Homer's ancient Greek epic about Odysseus, king of Ithaca, and his attempt to return home after the Trojan War.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b898dbb1-d6d5-4e0e-a0f2-7b9eabb37bdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Odysseus is married to Penelope, and they have a son named Telemachus. He leaves Ithaca to fight at Troy when Telemachus is still an infant. The war lasts ten years, and Odysseus's journey home takes another ten. By the time he returns, he has been gone for twenty years.
Odysseus is not the biggest or strongest warrior in Greek mythology. His strength is his mind. He is a strategist, a manipulator, a liar when necessary, and the man traditionally credited with devising the Trojan Horse.
Christopher Nolan's movie expands beyond the events of Homer's _Odyssey_ to show the end of the Trojan War. Greek soldiers hide inside the horse while Sinon, played by Elliot Page, helps deceive the Trojans into believing it is an offering. The Trojans bring it through the city's walls, allowing the Greeks to attack Troy from inside.
But winning the war is only the beginning of Odysseus's real story.
Back in Ithaca, Penelope has spent twenty years protecting her family and holding together what remains of Odysseus's household. Telemachus has grown into a young man without his father. Suitors have flooded into their home, consuming their food, abusing their hospitality, corrupting people around them, and pressuring Penelope to choose a new husband.
The suitors are not merely obnoxious guests. They are exploiting _xenia_ , the sacred Greek law of hospitality associated with Zeus. People were expected to welcome strangers and treat guests properly because they never knew when a god might arrive in disguise.
The suitors take that sacred obligation and weaponize it. They use a custom meant to create trust as permission to consume Odysseus's household from within.
Meanwhile, Odysseus is trying to return home through gods, monsters, temptations, grief, bad decisions, and the consequences of war. His journey is not only physical. It is mental, emotional, spiritual, and strategic. He is not simply trying to reach Ithaca. He is trying to figure out whether the man who left Ithaca twenty years earlier still exists.
* * *
## The Movie Was Declared Woke Before Anyone Saw It
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The political backlash started months before the movie was released.
People attacked Elliot Page's casting, often while falsely claiming he was playing Achilles or some massive Spartan warrior. Page actually plays Sinon, a smaller and more vulnerable figure whose importance comes from deception and sacrifice, not physical dominance.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aecb023b-be8f-4082-990b-c17c78649d85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Elliot Page as Sinon
Lupita Nyong'o's casting as Helen of Troy created even more outrage. She is Black, rather than the blonde, white version of Helen that many people have come to expect from Western paintings and previous movies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bd400528-c5ce-4abf-aa0f-7e0f3a0e2c24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Lupita Nyong'o's as Helen of Troy
Suddenly, half the internet became experts on Bronze Age Greece. People were debating armor, ships, ethnicity, masculinity, historical accuracy, Greek mythology, and the supposed destruction of Western civilization.
The backlash reached the point where people were saying Nolan had lost the plot. They claimed he had sold out to woke Hollywood, intentionally disrespected Western culture, and made casting decisions to appease some imaginary DEI committee at the Academy Awards.
Matt Walsh joined the pile-on before the movie was released and continued afterward. He called the casting "atrocious" and described Odysseus as an "anachronistic whiney, solemn shell of a man" plagued by trauma and guilt. According to Walsh, Nolan had taken one of history's great warriors and transformed him into a modern victim.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5caa9de6-9122-4105-8e49-148efcd95341?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Matt Walsh the Epitome of Piece of Shit
Honestly, some of it almost got to me.
I watched the videos. I read the arguments. I listened to people confidently explain why this movie was going to be a disaster. I went into the theater wondering whether Christopher Nolan had finally made a massive mistake.
He did not.
* * *
## Christopher Nolan Understood the Assignment
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This movie is absolutely epic.
Is the cast diverse? Yes.
Does that damage the story? No. Actually, it might be more accurate.
The ancient Mediterranean was not an isolated neighborhood where nobody ever encountered people from somewhere else. It was a center of trade, migration, conquest, slavery, commerce, and travel. More importantly, this is a mythological adaptation involving gods, monsters, prophecies, and divine intervention.
Casting still has to make sense within a story. I do not believe every actor automatically fits every role. Physicality matters when the story requires physicality.
But that is precisely why Page's casting works. Sinon is not presented as an unstoppable warrior beating men twice his size. He is smaller, vulnerable, expendable, and essential to Odysseus's plan. The character demonstrates that wars are not won only through strength. They are also won through deception, sacrifice, strategy, and the willingness to use human beings as pieces on a board.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f76ad85e-cc7e-4f2b-b49b-48feadbb8707?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The scenes inside the Trojan Horse are brutal. The men are packed together, drowning as the tide rises, pissing and shitting on one another, waiting for the slightest opportunity to escape and open the gates.
There is nothing glamorous about it. Nolan does not present war as a beautiful procession of muscular men marching heroically into battle. He shows what victory costs and what leaders sometimes ask other people to endure in order to achieve it.
Nyong'o's Helen does not destroy the story either. Her casting changes nothing about the deception, betrayal, heartbreak, or consequences surrounding Troy. Her relatively limited role also becomes important to Odysseus because her experience helps him think through how he might return to Ithaca without immediately revealing himself.
* * *
## This Is a Story About Masculinity
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I do not understand the argument that showing Odysseus wrestling with trauma somehow demasculates him.
If anything, that is what makes his masculinity believable.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f8e5671-b7f4-4a79-a316-18b8c3d481f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Matt Damon as Odysseus
This is not an Arnold Schwarzenegger movie where the hero kills everyone, delivers a one-liner, and walks away untouched. Odysseus spends ten years at war and another ten trying to return home. He watches men die. He sends some of them to their deaths. He makes impossible choices, loses people he loves, and carries the responsibility of leadership long after the glory of victory disappears.
That changes him.
Strength is not the absence of grief, guilt, doubt, or fear. Strength is carrying those things without allowing them to completely destroy you. It is finding a reason to continue when the mission that once defined you is over and the person you were before the war no longer exists.
That is the deeper question behind Odysseus's journey. Winning the war does not mean he knows how to come home. Victory gives him glory, but it does not give him peace. He still has to decide whether he wants to remain a warrior forever or return to being a husband, father, and king.
That is not a weak man. That is a man being forced to confront the full consequences of what he has done and what has been done to him.
* * *
## Leadership Does Not Mean Control
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The movie also understands something important about leadership: being responsible for people does not mean you can control them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a3eac369-d87c-4858-8e39-a2c98f642699?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Odysseus can warn his men. He can plan for them. He can try to protect them. He can understand the consequences better than they do. But he cannot make every decision for them.
His men slaughter the sacred cattle of Helios after being explicitly warned not to touch them. Odysseus does not choose that outcome, but he still has to live with the consequences.
That is one of the hardest parts of leadership. You can know the danger. You can explain it clearly. You can see exactly where a decision will lead, and people can still make it anyway.
Foreknowledge is not control.
Odysseus also has to decide who will be placed in danger and who may have to die. Leaders can pretend every person will come home, but that is not true. Sometimes every available choice is terrible. Sometimes there is no heroic answer that leaves everyone alive and morally clean.
The scenes involving the Underworld and the people Odysseus lost are powerful because they force him to confront the human cost behind his own choices. History may remember the victory. He remembers the faces.
Glory is temporary. The burden is not.
* * *
## Addiction, Comfort, and the Temptation to Stop Moving
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The movie also made me think about addiction.
The lotus and Calypso are separate parts of Odysseus's journey, but both represent different versions of the temptation to stop moving forward. The lotus offers forgetfulness. Calypso offers comfort, pleasure, and escape.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7241cb10-18c8-4131-b009-d5c49fbb5071?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Charlize Theron as Calypso
After everything Odysseus has endured, that temptation makes complete sense.
It made me think about soldiers who return from war and drink too much, use drugs, or find some other way to numb themselves. Not because they are weak, but because forgetting can feel easier than living with the people they lost and the choices they made.
Addiction can become its own island. You are no longer trapped by a monster or a god. You are trapped by the comfort of not having to remember.
Odysseus cannot return home until he is willing to leave that comfort and face his past. He has to remember his family, accept what happened to his crew, and resume the journey knowing that returning home will not erase what came before.
He cannot become the person he was before the war. He can only decide what kind of person he will be after it.
* * *
## We Are Being Fed Our Opinions
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The response to this movie made me think about something larger than _The Odyssey_.
We are being given our opinions before we are given the facts.
We see a clip, headline, screenshot, meme, AI-generated image, or reaction video. Someone packages an argument into a sound bite, and people repeat it to prove they are informed and on the correct team.
I see it constantly on Substack and Facebook. People respond to something I wrote with an argument that has almost nothing to do with what I said because they are not responding to me. They are responding with a prepackaged set of talking points somebody else gave them.
It almost worked on me with this movie.
The outrage was repeated so confidently and so often that I entered the theater wondering whether the movie might be an intentional attack on Western culture. Millions of people reached conclusions about the film before they had watched it or even knew which characters the actors were playing.
Sometimes I think that we are living in a simulation and that some massive artificial intelligence took control of the algorithms around the COVID era. I do not know if there is one person or force controlling it. But I do know what the incentives are producing.
The algorithms reward anger, certainty, humiliation, tribalism, and the quickest possible reaction. They do not reward thoughtfulness, restraint, curiosity, or admitting that you do not have enough information yet.
We are living in a post-truth society where the person who tells the most emotionally satisfying story often beats the person who has the facts.
The reaction to _The Odyssey_ allowed me to watch that process unfold on a compressed timeline. A narrative was created. People repeated it. The movie came out. The narrative was contradicted, and many people simply refused to reconsider it.
Admitting you were wrong is apparently no longer an option. Shit even Ben Shapiro liked it!
[](https://substack.com/redirect/967c723f-256e-4abb-a22f-1d8c4f5a17e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## When Norms Collapse, Darkness Gets In
The most political part of _The Odyssey_ may not be its casting. It may be what the story says about the collapse of norms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02cf42f8-a19b-4b36-a32e-56bbdec48163?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Antinous: A Bitch Ass Suitor**
Odysseus is gone for twenty years, ten years fighting at Troy and ten years trying to return. The darkness that spreads during that absence is not caused only by war, monsters, tragedy, and the anger of the gods.
It is also caused by people abandoning the laws and customs that hold society together.
The suitors understand the rules of hospitality. They exploit those rules while violating their purpose. They technically arrive as guests, but then consume the household, threaten Telemachus, pressure Penelope, corrupt the servants, and turn hospitality into occupation.
That is what makes their behavior so corrosive. They are not attacking the system from outside. They are hollowing it out from within.
A functioning society cannot survive through written law alone. There must also be shared standards about honesty, dignity, restraint, loyalty, hospitality, and acceptable behavior. There will always be things people can legally do that still destroy trust and weaken the culture around them.
In Homer's world, those standards are connected to Zeus and the gods. In another culture, they might be described as religious or biblical principles. But you do not have to believe in Zeus or belong to any religion to understand why they are necessary.
Over the past decade, we have watched social media push our culture toward the lowest possible denominator. The most dishonest, cruel, humiliating, degenerate, and attention-seeking behavior gets rewarded. The person willing to break the norm gets the attention, and everyone else begins lowering their own standards because they do not want to compete at a disadvantage.
Then comes the whataboutism.
Why should we tell the truth when the other side lies? Why should we follow the rules when they break them? Why should we maintain standards when they have already stooped lower?
Eventually, nobody is defending the norm. Everyone is only explaining why the other side forced them to abandon it.
That is how a culture collapses. Not necessarily through one dramatic event, but through millions of smaller choices where people decide that truth is optional and rules only matter when they can be used against someone else.
The consequences eventually reach everyone. That is the warning running beneath _The Odyssey_. When shared rules disappear, brute strength, deception, revenge, and violence rush in to replace them.
* * *
## My Review
[Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/07f51783-8f7d-4e35-9085-0a16c5bee14d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I give Christopher Nolan's _The Odyssey_ a 9 out of 10.
It is not perfect. Every movie has flaws if you look hard enough. People will debate the historical inaccuracies, changes to Homer, characters Nolan added, elements he removed, the costumes, ships, accents, casting, and everything else.
Fine.
But I walked out thinking, this is exactly why I still pay to see a movie in a theater.
It is visually stunning, thoughtful, violent, emotional, and much deeper than the culture-war argument surrounding it. It does not demasculate Odysseus. It gives masculinity weight. It shows that being a man is not about being untouched by war, grief, or failure. Crying because you miss you family. Praying for your fellow soldiers. Struck by fear to make a wrong choice. It is about how you carry those things and whether you can still find your way home.
It is a story about leadership without complete control, victory without peace, addiction as escape, family as purpose, and the terrible cost of decisions that cannot be undone.
It is also a warning about what happens when the shared laws, customs, and expectations holding a society together become nothing more than loopholes for selfish people to exploit.
Christopher Nolan understood the assignment.
Go see it.

It is about masculinity, addiction, leadership, and what happens when the norms holding society together collapse. | | and | Jul 21 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | Spoiler Warning I just got back from seeing Christopher Nolan's adaptation of The Odyssey , and I have a lot to say about it. This review contains spoilers. If you have not seen the movie, close this article, go watch it, and come back. I do not want to hear anybody complaining that I spoiled it for them. | | ---|---|--- I would also recommend learning the basic story of The Odyssey before watching the movie. You do not need to read Homer's entire epic, but a quick overview will make the characters, mythology, and structure much easier to follow. I am going to do three things here: First , explain the basic story. Second , talk about the political backlash surrounding the movie. Finally , explain why I think Nolan's The Odyssey is a 9 out of 10 epic about war, masculinity, addiction, leadership, and what happens when the norms holding a society together begin to collapse. What Is The Odyssey? The Odyssey is Homer's ancient Greek epic about Odysseus, king of Ithaca, and his attempt to return home after the Trojan War. Odysseus is married to Penelope, and they have a son named Telemachus. He leaves Ithaca to fight at Troy when Telemachus is still an infant. The war lasts ten years, and Odysseus's journey home takes another ten. By the time he returns, he has been gone for twenty years. Odysseus is not the biggest or strongest warrior in Greek mythology. His strength is his mind. He is a strategist, a manipulator, a liar when necessary, and the man traditionally credited with devising the Trojan Horse. Christopher Nolan's movie expands beyond the events of Homer's Odyssey to show the end of the Trojan War. Greek soldiers hide inside the horse while Sinon, played by Elliot Page, helps deceive the Trojans into believing it is an offering. The Trojans bring it through the city's walls, allowing the Greeks to attack Troy from inside. But winning the war is only the beginning of Odysseus's real story. Back in Ithaca, Penelope has spent twenty years protecting her family and holding together what remains of Odysseus's household. Telemachus has grown into a young man without his father. Suitors have flooded into their home, consuming their food, abusing their hospitality, corrupting people around them, and pressuring Penelope to choose a new husband. The suitors are not merely obnoxious guests. They are exploiting xenia , the sacred Greek law of hospitality associated with Zeus. People were expected to welcome strangers and treat guests properly because they never knew when a god might arrive in disguise. The suitors take that sacred obligation and weaponize it. They use a custom meant to create trust as permission to consume Odysseus's household from within. Meanwhile, Odysseus is trying to return home through gods, monsters, temptations, grief, bad decisions, and the consequences of war. His journey is not only physical. It is mental, emotional, spiritual, and strategic. He is not simply trying to reach Ithaca. He is trying to figure out whether the man who left Ithaca twenty years earlier still exists. The Movie Was Declared Woke Before Anyone Saw It The political backlash started months before the movie was released. People attacked Elliot Page's casting, often while falsely claiming he was playing Achilles or some massive Spartan warrior. Page actually plays Sinon, a smaller and more vulnerable figure whose importance comes from deception and sacrifice, not physical dominance. | | ---|---|--- Elliot Page as Sinon Lupita Nyong'o's casting as Helen of Troy created even more outrage. She is Black, rather than the blonde, white version of Helen that many people have come to expect from Western paintings and previous movies. | | ---|---|--- Lupita Nyong'o's as Helen of Troy Suddenly, half the internet became experts on Bronze Age Greece. People were debating armor, ships, ethnicity, masculinity, historical accuracy, Greek mythology, and the supposed destruction of Western civilization. The backlash reached the point where people were saying Nolan had lost the plot. They claimed he had sold out to woke Hollywood, intentionally disrespected Western culture, and made casting decisions to appease some imaginary DEI committee at the Academy Awards. Matt Walsh joined the pile-on before the movie was released and continued afterward. He called the casting "atrocious" and described Odysseus as an "anachronistic whiney, solemn shell of a man" plagued by trauma and guilt. According to Walsh, Nolan had taken one of history's great warriors and transformed him into a modern victim. | | ---|---|--- Matt Walsh the Epitome of Piece of Shit Honestly, some of it almost got to me. I watched the videos. I read the arguments. I listened to people confidently explain why this movie was going to be a disaster. I went into the theater wondering whether Christopher Nolan had finally made a massive mistake. He did not. Christopher Nolan Understood the Assignment This movie is absolutely epic. Is the cast diverse? Yes. Does that damage the story? No. Actually, it might be more accurate. The ancient Mediterranean was not an isolated neighborhood where nobody ever encountered people from somewhere else. It was a center of trade, migration, conquest, slavery, commerce, and travel. More importantly, this is a mythological adaptation involving gods, monsters, prophecies, and divine intervention. Casting still has to make sense within a story. I do not believe every actor automatically fits every role. Physicality matters when the story requires physicality. But that is precisely why Page's casting works. Sinon is not presented as an unstoppable warrior beating men twice his size. He is smaller, vulnerable, expendable, and essential to Odysseus's plan. The character demonstrates that wars are not won only through strength. They are also won through deception, sacrifice, strategy, and the willingness to use human beings as pieces on a board. | | ---|---|--- The scenes inside the Trojan Horse are brutal. The men are packed together, drowning as the tide rises, pissing and shitting on one another, waiting for the slightest opportunity to escape and open the gates. There is nothing glamorous about it. Nolan does not present war as a beautiful procession of muscular men marching heroically into battle. He shows what victory costs and what leaders sometimes ask other people to endure in order to achieve it. Nyong'o's Helen does not destroy the story either. Her casting changes nothing about the deception, betrayal, heartbreak, or consequences surrounding Troy. Her relatively limited role also becomes important to Odysseus because her experience helps him think through how he might return to Ithaca without immediately revealing himself. This Is a Story About Masculinity I do not understand the argument that showing Odysseus wrestling with trauma somehow demasculates him. If anything, that is what makes his masculinity believable. | | ---|---|--- Matt Damon as Odysseus This is not an Arnold Schwarzenegger movie where the hero kills everyone, delivers a one-liner, and walks away untouched. Odysseus spends ten years at war and another ten trying to return home. He watches men die. He sends some of them to their deaths. He makes impossible choices, loses people he loves, and carries the responsibility of leadership long after the glory of victory disappears. That changes him. Strength is not the absence of grief, guilt, doubt, or fear. Strength is carrying those things without allowing them to completely destroy you. It is finding a reason to continue when the mission that once defined you is over and the person you were before the war no longer exists. That is the deeper question behind Odysseus's journey. Winning the war does not mean he knows how to come home. Victory gives him glory, but it does not give him peace. He still has to decide whether he wants to remain a warrior forever or return to being a husband, father, and king. That is not a weak man. That is a man being forced to confront the full consequences of what he has done and what has been done to him. Leadership Does Not Mean Control The movie also understands something important about leadership: being responsible for people does not mean you can control them. | | ---|---|--- Odysseus can warn his men. He can plan for them. He can try to protect them. He can understand the consequences better than they do. But he cannot make every decision for them. His men slaughter the sacred cattle of Helios after being explicitly warned not to touch them. Odysseus does not choose that outcome, but he still has to live with the consequences. That is one of the hardest parts of leadership. You can know the danger. You can explain it clearly. You can see exactly where a decision will lead, and people can still make it anyway. Foreknowledge is not control. Odysseus also has to decide who will be placed in danger and who may have to die. Leaders can pretend every person will come home, but that is not true. Sometimes every available choice is terrible. Sometimes there is no heroic answer that leaves everyone alive and morally clean. The scenes involving the Underworld and the people Odysseus lost are powerful because they force him to confront the human cost behind his own choices. History may remember the victory. He remembers the faces. Glory is temporary. The burden is not. Addiction, Comfort, and the Temptation to Stop Moving The movie also made me think about addiction. The lotus and Calypso are separate parts of Odysseus's journey, but both represent different versions of the temptation to stop moving forward. The lotus offers forgetfulness. Calypso offers comfort, pleasure, and escape. | | ---|---|--- Charlize Theron as Calypso After everything Odysseus has endured, that temptation makes complete sense. It made me think about soldiers who return from war and drink too much, use drugs, or find some other way to numb themselves. Not because they are weak, but because forgetting can feel easier than living with the people they lost and the choices they made. Addiction can become its own island. You are no longer trapped by a monster or a god. You are trapped by the comfort of not having to remember. Odysseus cannot return home until he is willing to leave that comfort and face his past. He has to remember his family, accept what happened to his crew, and resume the journey knowing that returning home will not erase what came before. He cannot become the person he was before the war. He can only decide what kind of person he will be after it. We Are Being Fed Our Opinions The response to this movie made me think about something larger than The Odyssey. We are being given our opinions before we are given the facts. We see a clip, headline, screenshot, meme, AI-generated image, or reaction video. Someone packages an argument into a sound bite, and people repeat it to prove they are informed and on the correct team. I see it constantly on Substack and Facebook. People respond to something I wrote with an argument that has almost nothing to do with what I said because they are not responding to me. They are responding with a prepackaged set of talking points somebody else gave them. It almost worked on me with this movie. The outrage was repeated so confidently and so often that I entered the theater wondering whether the movie might be an intentional attack on Western culture. Millions of people reached conclusions about the film before they had watched it or even knew which characters the actors were playing. Sometimes I think that we are living in a simulation and that some massive artificial intelligence took control of the algorithms around the COVID era. I do not know if there is one person or force controlling it. But I do know what the incentives are producing. The algorithms reward anger, certainty, humiliation, tribalism, and the quickest possible reaction. They do not reward thoughtfulness, restraint, curiosity, or admitting that you do not have enough information yet. We are living in a post-truth society where the person who tells the most emotionally satisfying story often beats the person who has the facts. The reaction to The Odyssey allowed me to watch that process unfold on a compressed timeline. A narrative was created. People repeated it. The movie came out. The narrative was contradicted, and many people simply refused to reconsider it. Admitting you were wrong is apparently no longer an option. Shit even Ben Shapiro liked it! When Norms Collapse, Darkness Gets In The most political part of The Odyssey may not be its casting. It may be what the story says about the collapse of norms. | | ---|---|--- Antinous: A Bitch Ass Suitor Odysseus is gone for twenty years, ten years fighting at Troy and ten years trying to return. The darkness that spreads during that absence is not caused only by war, monsters, tragedy, and the anger of the gods. It is also caused by people abandoning the laws and customs that hold society together. The suitors understand the rules of hospitality. They exploit those rules while violating their purpose. They technically arrive as guests, but then consume the household, threaten Telemachus, pressure Penelope, corrupt the servants, and turn hospitality into occupation. That is what makes their behavior so corrosive. They are not attacking the system from outside. They are hollowing it out from within. A functioning society cannot survive through written law alone. There must also be shared standards about honesty, dignity, restraint, loyalty, hospitality, and acceptable behavior. There will always be things people can legally do that still destroy trust and weaken the culture around them. In Homer's world, those standards are connected to Zeus and the gods. In another culture, they might be described as religious or biblical principles. But you do not have to believe in Zeus or belong to any religion to understand why they are necessary. Over the past decade, we have watched social media push our culture toward the lowest possible denominator. The most dishonest, cruel, humiliating, degenerate, and attention-seeking behavior gets rewarded. The person willing to break the norm gets the attention, and everyone else begins lowering their own standards because they do not want to compete at a disadvantage. Then comes the whataboutism. Why should we tell the truth when the other side lies? Why should we follow the rules when they break them? Why should we maintain standards when they have already stooped lower? Eventually, nobody is defending the norm. Everyone is only explaining why the other side forced them to abandon it. That is how a culture collapses. Not necessarily through one dramatic event, but through millions of smaller choices where people decide that truth is optional and rules only matter when they can be used against someone else. The consequences eventually reach everyone. That is the warning running beneath The Odyssey. When shared rules disappear, brute strength, deception, revenge, and violence rush in to replace them. My Review I give Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey a 9 out of 10. It is not perfect. Every movie has flaws if you look hard enough. People will debate the historical inaccuracies, changes to Homer, characters Nolan added, elements he removed, the costumes, ships, accents, casting, and everything else. Fine. But I walked out thinking, this is exactly why I still pay to see a movie in a theater. It is visually stunning, thoughtful, violent, emotional, and much deeper than the culture-war argument surrounding it. It does not demasculate Odysseus. It gives masculinity weight. It shows that being a man is not about being untouched by war, grief, or failure. Crying because you miss you family. Praying for your fellow soldiers. Struck by fear to make a wrong choice. It is about how you carry those things and whether you can still find your way home. It is a story about leadership without complete control, victory without peace, addiction as escape, family as purpose, and the terrible cost of decisions that cannot be undone. It is also a warning about what happens when the shared laws, customs, and expectations holding a society together become nothing more than loopholes for selfish people to exploit. Christopher Nolan understood the assignment. Go see it. Stay Angry. p.s. Read my review of Andor as well. | | | | ---|---|--- | Jan 16 | Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS by supporting Matt's and Laura's work. ## Next250

| We celebrated America's 250th birthday the best way we know how - by preparing for the next 250.
This month, grassroots leaders from across Georgia came together at [Next250](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001n1R1F4bpNroN-YhmIgM9XQZzqKwB4-VYFsoNRw_yuExROsafKkCMKq1t_CwKx7gFskjVICvlWKBRkmX5ukgDpzZ0JX5T-U52HOAudCRP7QlpdCjRwzAWF5YTmEbYcixhlIE3sKZ3K3CA1gmZIGu9avzDV9Vga79aLEyeE7VkYm2e3efjpcbmPk7FWz6nM9gpM0lr3AszVNVe5tgDl7MVHFPbGYQvkttBI0DLZqMk7rjYNd0PFDU5dw==&c=X3ZMSKqWNAHdbyB606YeohxhUu2qIxm6J-0Ed2DaemwPmcDmy48Ntg==&ch=Cp4C-SCNRjsmDiSzwm7JZJs4e04BVnDW9zZ0ulF4LLvy-DohHqLaFQ==) to sharpen their skills, build stronger networks, and prepare for the challenges ahead. Through speakers, hands-on training, and practical breakout sessions covering everything from voter engagement and messaging to fundraising and organizing, attendees left better equipped to make a difference in their communities.
The next chapter of America's story will be written by citizens who are willing to lead. We're proud to invest in the people who will help keep Georgia, and our nation, moving forward for the next 250 years.

## [New Georgia Laws](https://fsdy8nbbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001n1R1F4bpNroN-YhmIgM9XQZzqKwB4-VYFsoNRw_yuExROsafKkCMKq1t_CwKx7gFzwyKCkVizS3_QU6ncgLO3dyby-HHOD7S-50IQyzmLbidTo77EZpVV5YoFS6pXOSMUEzCr-M-sN8TEiKx4mzBsoTGQdpu8V2i51EdILhZhFwCnYXJLs6APrchHqp7S82XlRhdnKVdyR_Pt-GbI___ZGsXYu7ZcqWDDrE_ALhne2VE6zS6LPbnzDXR1PY3ZQVWPKR-stlnvsKiJqtoCIqW_g==&c=X3ZMSKqWNAHdbyB606YeohxhUu2qIxm6J-0Ed2DaemwPmcDmy48Ntg==&ch=Cp4C-SCNRjsmDiSzwm7JZJs4e04BVnDW9zZ0ulF4LLvy-DohHqLaFQ==) Effective July 1st
---
| Each year, July 1 marks an important milestone in Georgia, as many of the bills passed during the legislative session officially become law.
Unless a bill specifies a different effective date, Georgia law takes effect on July 1, aligning with the start of the state's new fiscal year.
Family and Children: SB 433: Rio's Law (Sen. Brian Strickland) creates voluntary specialty "autism alert" license plates for people with autism and developmental disabilities, as well as their spouses, parents, or legal guardians.
HB 350: Safe Haven Baby Box Bill (Rep. Mike Cameron): expands Georgia's Safe Place for Newborns law by allowing parents in crisis to anonymously surrender newborns through secure "newborn safety devices" (often called baby boxes) at approved locations.
Public Safety: SB 570: Georgia Human Trafficking Prevention Training Act (Sen. Shawn Still): combats human trafficking and protects victims by requiring training for hotel and short-term rental employees to identify and report trafficking. The training equips them to recognize warning signs and properly report suspected cases to law enforcement or the National Human Trafficking Hotline.
HB 295: Property Owners Protection Act (Rep. Houston Gaines): holds local governments accountable by allowing property owners to file claims for compensation when cities or counties fail to enforce laws against public camping, loitering, panhandling, drug activity, shoplifting, or public nuisances - including violations of state immigration enforcement requirements (anti-sanctuary policies).
SB 591: Georgia Protecting Religious Services from Disruptive Protests (Sen. Steve Gooch): creates a prohibition targeting the intentional disruption of religious services and also adds similar protections for funerals or memorial services. This bill provides for enhanced penalties for such violations and aims to protect the peaceful exercise of religion.
Education: SB 552: The TPUSA Act (Sen. Ben Watson): strengthens free speech protections in Georgia public schools by ensuring students have equal access to form and participate in political or philosophical clubs during non-instructional time. It prohibits schools from discriminating against student speech or clubs based on viewpoint, while still allowing schools to maintain order and keep participation voluntary.
HB 1030: Math Matters Act (Rep. Sandy Donatucci): strengthens math education in Georgia public schools by requiring more instructional time, expanded access to advanced courses, and better-prepared teachers. Key provisions include mandating at least 60 minutes of daily core math instruction for 4th and 5th graders, automatic enrollment in advanced math classes for high-performing students (with parental opt-out), rigorous standards, and updated teacher certification.
Economic Relief: HB 463: Income Tax Relief (Rep. Shaw Blackmon): delivers meaningful, multi-year tax relief for Georgia families and workers by reducing the state's flat income tax rate from 5.19% to 4.99% starting in 2026, with further gradual reductions down to 3.99% over the following years if revenue targets are met.
HB 1344: The Georgia Insurance Affordability and Claims Integrity Act (Rep. Matt Reeves): delivers targeted reforms to lower insurance costs for Georgians by strengthening oversight of the insurance industry. The bill increases fines on insurers for violations, closes loopholes that allow uninsured drivers to operate other people's insured vehicles, and toughens penalties for insurance fraud to improve claims integrity and reduce fraud.

In the months ahead, Greater Georgia will be traveling the state, engaging communities, educating voters, and continuing to build the grassroots movement that will shape Georgia's future. From voter registration efforts and community events to leadership training and voter education, we're committed to ensuring Georgians have the information and opportunities they need to make their voices heard. | | | Next250 | We celebrated America's 250th birthday the best way we know how - by preparing for the next 250. This month, grassroots leaders from across Georgia came together at == to sharpen their skills, build stronger networks, and prepare for the challenges ahead. Through speakers, hands-on training, and practical breakout sessions covering everything from voter engagement and messaging to fundraising and organizing, attendees left better equipped to make a difference in their communities. The next chapter of America's story will be written by citizens who are willing to lead. We're proud to invest in the people who will help keep Georgia, and our nation, moving forward for the next 250 years. | | | | | | | | | | | | Legislative Awards One of the highlights of Next250 was recognizing a group of == whose leadership has made a meaningful difference for Georgia families. Our Legislative Leadership Awards celebrate lawmakers who have championed policies that expand opportunity, strengthen communities, protect individual liberty, and keep Georgia moving in the right direction. From advancing affordability and improving healthcare access to protecting election integrity and supporting economic growth, these leaders have demonstrated a steadfast commitment to serving the people of Georgia. We are grateful for their partnership and leadership under the Gold Dome, and we were proud to recognize their work alongside grassroots leaders from across the state who are committed to building a stronger Georgia. | | Rep. Katie Dempsey | | Rep. Matt Reeves | | Rep. Angie O'Steen | | Rep. Sandy Donatucci | | Sen. Chuck Payne | | Sen. Billy Hickman | | Sen. Max Burns | | Sen. Jason Dickerson | | | == Effective July 1st | Each year, July 1 marks an important milestone in Georgia, as many of the bills passed during the legislative session officially become law. Unless a bill specifies a different effective date, Georgia law takes effect on July 1, aligning with the start of the state's new fiscal year. Family and Children: SB 433: Rio's Law (Sen. Brian Strickland) creates voluntary specialty "autism alert" license plates for people with autism and developmental disabilities, as well as their spouses, parents, or legal guardians. HB 350: Safe Haven Baby Box Bill (Rep. Mike Cameron): expands Georgia's Safe Place for Newborns law by allowing parents in crisis to anonymously surrender newborns through secure "newborn safety devices" (often called baby boxes) at approved locations. Public Safety: SB 570: Georgia Human Trafficking Prevention Training Act (Sen. Shawn Still): combats human trafficking and protects victims by requiring training for hotel and short-term rental employees to identify and report trafficking. The training equips them to recognize warning signs and properly report suspected cases to law enforcement or the National Human Trafficking Hotline. HB 295: Property Owners Protection Act (Rep. Houston Gaines): holds local governments accountable by allowing property owners to file claims for compensation when cities or counties fail to enforce laws against public camping, loitering, panhandling, drug activity, shoplifting, or public nuisances - including violations of state immigration enforcement requirements (anti-sanctuary policies). SB 591: Georgia Protecting Religious Services from Disruptive Protests (Sen. Steve Gooch): creates a prohibition targeting the intentional disruption of religious services and also adds similar protections for funerals or memorial services. This bill provides for enhanced penalties for such violations and aims to protect the peaceful exercise of religion. Education: SB 552: The TPUSA Act (Sen. Ben Watson): strengthens free speech protections in Georgia public schools by ensuring students have equal access to form and participate in political or philosophical clubs during non-instructional time. It prohibits schools from discriminating against student speech or clubs based on viewpoint, while still allowing schools to maintain order and keep participation voluntary. HB 1030: Math Matters Act (Rep. Sandy Donatucci): strengthens math education in Georgia public schools by requiring more instructional time, expanded access to advanced courses, and better-prepared teachers. Key provisions include mandating at least 60 minutes of daily core math instruction for 4th and 5th graders, automatic enrollment in advanced math classes for high-performing students (with parental opt-out), rigorous standards, and updated teacher certification. Economic Relief: HB 463: Income Tax Relief (Rep. Shaw Blackmon): delivers meaningful, multi-year tax relief for Georgia families and workers by reducing the state's flat income tax rate from 5.19% to 4.99% starting in 2026, with further gradual reductions down to 3.99% over the following years if revenue targets are met. HB 1344: The Georgia Insurance Affordability and Claims Integrity Act (Rep. Matt Reeves): delivers targeted reforms to lower insurance costs for Georgians by strengthening oversight of the insurance industry. The bill increases fines on insurers for violations, closes loopholes that allow uninsured drivers to operate other people's insured vehicles, and toughens penalties for insurance fraud to improve claims integrity and reduce fraud. | | | In the Field | Our team had a great time tabling at the Suwannee Porch Fest, the Cobb County Republican Party's 250th Celebration, and Alive After 5 in Roswell! name: Melanie Lucero For Congress
subject: The part they cut from my interview
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MELANIE LUCERO FOR CONGRESS
body:
It happened inside my own family. Here's what I'll do about it in Congress.
| [ MELANIE LUCERO
FOR CONGRESS · VIRGINIA'S 5TH DISTRICT ](https://us.list-manage.com/VL49MG9cvrt?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)
---
Where I stand · Border security
# Illegal immigration isn't a talking point in my house. It's a scar.
Peter,When I was growing up, my father entered an arranged marriage to an illegal alien. What followed was abuse, financial fraud, and identity theft — and a government that looked the other way while my family paid the price.And when I interview with left-leaning news media and spend 15 or 20 minutes telling them the horrors and realities of what illegal immigration can do to a family, here's what makes it into their story: _" She has strong beliefs regarding immigration."_ Not one word of what I experienced.So when politicians shrug at open borders, I take it personally. And when President Trump says _build the wall_ , I don't flinch — I ask where to report for duty.But I've also seen immigration done right. In the Marine Corps, I served alongside men and women from other countries who earned their citizenship in an American uniform. They are some of the most patriotic people I've ever met — they know exactly what our flag stands for and what this country was founded on, because they raised their right hand and swore to defend it. And believe me: no one resents illegal immigration more than the men and women who earned their citizenship the right way.In Congress, I'll vote to finish the wall, fully fund ICE, empower Border Patrol agents to do their jobs, and fight to cut off every federal dollar flowing to sanctuary cities. No exceptions, no loopholes, no one bypassing the legal path to citizenship.You shouldn't have to wonder whether your representative means it. I've lived it. | [Read My Border Plan](https://us.list-manage.com/13xj8gXbF3R?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04)
---
Takes two minutes. No forms, no pop-ups — just where I stand.
* * *
For the 5th,
Melanie Lucero
Marine Veteran · Republican for Congress, VA-05
**P.S.** If you want a border-security conservative who has lived this fight — not just polled it — [chip in to help us finish these last 12 days strong](https://us.list-manage.com/12frFAmH4v6?e=b859d69a85&c2id=840d926fa883d6ae62831c5dde7f0f04).

They are some of the most patriotic people I've ever met — they know exactly what our flag stands for and what this country was founded on, because they raised their right hand and swore to defend it. And believe me: no one resents illegal immigration more than the men and women who earned their citizenship the right way.In Congress, I'll vote to finish the wall, fully fund ICE, empower Border Patrol agents to do their jobs, and fight to cut off every federal dollar flowing to sanctuary cities. No exceptions, no loopholes, no one bypassing the legal path to citizenship.You shouldn't have to wonder whether your representative means it. I've lived it. | Takes two minutes. No forms, no pop-ups — just where I stand. For the 5th, Melanie Lucero Marine Veteran · Republican for Congress, VA-05 P.S. subject: I will not hide from Texans
body:
Greg Abbott refuses to take accountability for the damage he has done to Texans, but I will take a stand.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Texans deserve a governor who's willing to answer for their record, Peter.
I've made it clear that I'm ready to debate Greg Abbott — but he’s stayed silent. There’s a very simple reason why:
**He’s failed Texans, and he doesn’t want to actually face them.**
Texans have faced years of rising costs, some of the highest uninsured rates in the country, families struggling to keep the lights on because electricity has become so expensive, and billions of our taxpayer dollars flowing to politically connected donors and special interests instead of working people. **Greg Abbott should be openly willing to defend his record before the people he serves.**
Instead, he's refusing to face voters — _but I wouldn’t do that._
I'm running for governor because I believe leadership means showing up, answering tough questions, and being accountable to the people of Texas. Not hiding from them.
I'll proudly defend my vision to strengthen our public schools, lower costs for working families, expand access to healthcare, and build an economy that works for _everyone_ — not just the wealthy and well-connected.
Greg Abbott can keep avoiding the conversation.
But I'll keep traveling across Texas, listening to voters, and earning their trust.

Flabby, burnt-okra-colored miscreant Donald Trump finally accomplished some history: he united Canada. Unfortunately, as Dean pointed out, he united Canada _against us_.
Trump's stupid tariffs, emotionally perforated poodle-barking threats, and endless attempts to turn our closest ally into a punching bag have finally pushed Canadian leaders from a position of polite disapproval into more of a "suck-it, poutine-hater" stance. Dean laid it all out and as much as it's unpleasant in many ways, it was hard for all of us not to break out laughing at Trump (and so we did).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2a9888d7-3c9c-488a-b18a-d25a118b2847?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Provinces are yanking U.S booze from their shelves. Officials are considering retaliatory tariffs and boycotts involving energy, potash, and critical minerals. Even conservative members of provincial governments are openly mocking this imbecilic empty-egg-carton of a man. Canadians are famously kind people--but, as Dean reminded us, "nice" doesn't mean *willing to be kicked in the privates by a demented Florida grifter tweeting from his golden sh*tter at 2am.*
Trump assumes every country will surrender if he creates enough chaos. You'd think that no country has done so would be a hint by now. They know--as any sentient human does--there's no agreement to be reached with the convicted felon. He breaks treaties, invents deals that exist in the same way "they're eating the dogs, eating the cats," and will change course after flattery from a dictator. If a billionaire waves money and he catches a clear scent, he'd kick Barron over to get to it, deal be damned.
Canada increasingly gets what far too many American institutions can't digest: Trump can't negotiate in good faith because _piles of human excrement tend not to be infused with it_. He wants drama, submission, personal profit. Dean laughingly pointed out Canada's lighting Trump's playbook on fire because they get that its willingness to impose real economic consequences may be the only language Trump understands.
Trump thought he could bully Canada without consequences. But what Canada is preparing to do next could hit him--and MAGA--exactly where it hurts. Please become a paid subscriber to see how Canada is making Trump pay, and why Trump's Saudi nuclear deal should terrify us...

I testified before the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC) of the United States Senate regarding "Fraud in America."

| [ ](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq)

Dear Patriot,
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq)When I started undercover investigative journalism as a college student at Rutgers, I pored over the history of journalism. I studied the techniques of great authors who broke stories that transformed America. From Stetson Kennedy, who infiltrated the highest echelons of the KKK in the 1940s, to Upton Sinclair, who went undercover in the 1900s working in a meatpacking plant in Chicago. Sinclair's book, The Jungle, resulted in a national uproar over food safety and the creation of what is now the Food and Drug Administration. Every notable author and journalist who came before me used similar tactics to get the story: fearless boots on the ground. And as I've found in my nearly 20 years as a journalist, my job is limited to what I can see and record through public access . . . undercover or not. At the end of each investigation, I'm left wanting more. I can see the threads dangling in front of me, waiting to be pulled, but accessible only to law enforcement and their powers to investigate. **But now, the world has shifted . . .** I testified before the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee (HSGAC) of the United States Senate regarding "Fraud in America." Following my opening remarks, where I expressed my limits as a journalist, something extraordinary happened. **Committee Chairman Rand Paul invited me to submit requests for subpoenas to his office.** Notably, Senator Paul, as the chairman of HSGAC, is the only member of the Senate with **unilateral authority** to issue subpoenas. From Upton Sinclair to Woodward and Bernstein, the model for action has been: **Journalist publishes → Institution reacts.** After my testimony before the Senate, that model will be inverted . . . **at least temporarily.** Power shifts. Rules change. **Doors close.** That's why we have to [**move fast**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq), and I need your help more than ever to take advantage of an unprecedented offer. I'm putting together a small team of researchers who can pull those dangling threads left from current and previously closed investigations.
* We can follow the money trails to see who is truly behind the fraudulent ballots.
* We have a shot at unraveling the global web of money that funds illegal immigration.
* We finally have a chance to see the documents behind Pfizer's illegal "Gain of Function" research on COVID-19.

**At the bottom of every rabbit hole is a lock box filled with receipts.** Senator Paul has handed us a golden key. [**Will you help me fund this new squad?**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq) Remember, Al Capone was brought down by an accountant. In today's dollars, Capone's criminal enterprise was worth $2 billion. Taxpayers are being defrauded of at least **$250 billion every year** on the federal level alone — money out of your pocket, counted against your vote. And at the Senate hearing on Fraud in America, our elected officials admitted that the governmental bodies tasked with stopping fraud for decades are wholly ineffective. That leaves us to do the job. Are you in? [**Help me and my team get to work.**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq) We have HUNDREDS of Al Capones to take down who have been ripping all of us off and stealing our national treasure . . . and our votes. **Time is short.**[**Please help me and my team get started today.**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq) Thank you for all that you do.
In Truth,James O'KeefeFounder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. I'm still grasping the impact of the Senate hearing. Most journalists might just smile and say "thank you" if Senator Paul asked them to submit subpoena requests to him. But those journalists have not gone as deep as I have. They haven't risked their lives. Some never leave the comfort of their office. I know what the offer means. I've lived with the frustration of knowing that the true players behind an operation can hide in darkness. With your help, OMG is taking advantage of this immediately — until the door closes. [**Please help fund this rapid response team today.**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyUkbuOrDAMhp8mdKBcuBYpjoTo5rRbIpOYEC25iCSzr79iVlNttaV_f_5kyx-P9QH2tN78B4fSprReac0HGnB4QFIHeIN65ZT3NR1qLlZQ2T5xbaHSsuNs3McKJRvGdmQ9E6w6pBAK9o11Su8b4tTqDliH0wgbh57SrrLy9tGBC9ayjk8N13pi20g3trd654y0tEQNGRvrk9WYVAgxhtNmq1ITLlOd8sg5JiL-Eb4QviRU5cIGPOqQGxUc4Uv4RNzRobZgrlDiHTlTX-B1ncoWA3qo3VbHEIGIpWS3plAuhUTMv0DC-xu4bcURMb-GfjIFLoI1noj5fde7E3xGn4mYbUqE9-BCeZWiqy6p45c9T5v6gbTUOLDnvXiV__iGp-TfAQAA__9z_Zcq)

name: Raquel, Virginians for Reproductive Freedom
subject: I almost didn’t have the family I always dreamed of
body:
https://va4reprofreedom.org/ [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
Friend,
For me, reproductive freedom isn’t theoretical.
At 30 years old, I was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Doctors told me the treatments I needed to save my life would also give me a 98% chance of infertility .
I beat cancer. And then I defied the odds. I became the proud mother of my amazing daughter, Marisol.
Raquel's family [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSM01/1/118960/images/Disney%20Dream%202022.jpeg]
When I look at her, I see everything cancer tried to take from me and didn’t. And I think about all the families who deserve the same opportunity to make their own decisions with their doctors about building the family they want.
Because I know what it feels like to be a high-risk patient trying to navigate a pregnancy in an uncertain legal environment. I lived that fear right here in Virginia, when there were real proposals that would have criminalized the care a cancer survivor like me might need.
No one should have to worry whether a politician will stand between them and the healthcare they need.
That’s why I proudly support this historic campaign to enshrine reproductive freedom into Virginia’s Constitution once and for all. I want to ensure future families in Virginia can make decisions with their doctors, just as I could. I want to ensure my daughter Marisol can make these decisions for herself.
On November 3, that is why I am voting YES on #1.
Will you make a contribution today to help us rally more Virginians to vote YES on #1 on Election Day?
YES, COUNT ME IN! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=072326]
I’m so proud to be a part of this historic moment. I hope you’ll join me.
In solidarity,
Raquel, Mom & Advocate

body:
Democracy needs our courage
---
| |
---
**Everything about this campaign just got bigger. ** This week, two men showed up at campaign HQ and said: Can you sign for a _big_ sign delivery? For a second, I thought they meant they had a large number of signs, which makes sense because we're flying through yard signs about as fast as we can order them. But what they meant was they had a BIG sign delivery. We've got one hundred 4x4 signs and twenty-seven 4x8 signs ready to go up across East Tennessee on highways, front yards in front of highly trafficked roads, and busy corners where thousands of our neighbors will encounter our campaign for the first time. (And if you think those don't sound **_that_** big, take a gander at the photo below. I have never seen my face that large!)
---
|
---
We spent a lot of time thinking about what we wanted to say to folks encountering our campaign for the first time, and we realized it's something we talk a lot about as a team: **_Democracy Needs Our Courage_** If you voted for Trump**** once, twice, or three times, but are starting to think you were sold a false bill of goods, democracy needs _your_ courage. If you're a lifelong Dem ground down by years of voting for change that hasn't showed up yet, democracy needs _your_ courage. If you've never voted at all because you used to think it didn't matter, democracy needs _your_ courage, too. We don't all have to do everything, but we do all have to do something. Thank you for being part of this campaign of courage.

name: Conroy for Congress
subject: Greg Landsman Votes Against Banning Congressional Stock Trading — After Getting Caught Violating the STOCK Act Himself
body:
Conroy: Landsman claims to lead the charge against congressional stock trading — today he voted to protect it

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/HZFJvVxFZdr?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)
| | | | | |

**Greg Landsman Votes Against Banning Congressional Stock Trading — After Getting Caught Violating the STOCK Act Himself** _Conroy: Landsman claims to lead the charge against congressional stock trading — today he voted to protect it_**CINCINNATI, OH** — Yesterday, Congressman Greg Landsman voted against H.R. 7008, legislation that bans members of Congress from buying individual stocks and requires photo identification to vote in federal elections. The bill passed the House 232–198 without Landsman's support.With one vote, Landsman rejected two commonsense reforms Ohioans overwhelmingly support: proving who you are before you cast a ballot and stopping politicians rom using insider information to enrich themselves playing the stock market. **The hypocrisy speaks for itself.** Landsman has spent years telling voters he is leading the fight to stop members of Congress from trading stocks, even cutting campaign ads railing against congressional insider trading. But in 2024, Landsman was forced to admit he failed to disclose more than 90 stock trades on time, worth as much as $1.6 million, what a government ethics expert at Public Citizen called a violation of the STOCK Act. The trades included holdings in oil, pharmaceutical, and big tech companies — the very industries Landsman attacks in public while profiting from in private and overseeing on the Energy and Commerce Committee.**Wrong on election integrity, too.** Ohio already requires photo ID to vote, and it works. Roughly 8 in 10 Americans support voter ID. Yesterday, Greg Landsman voted to block that basic safeguard from protecting every federal election in America.Eric Conroy, CIA veteran, Air Force intelligence officer, and Republican nominee for Congress in Ohio's First District, released the following statement:_“I spent my career serving this country. Greg Landsman has spent his career serving himself. He looks into the camera and tells you he's cleaning up Congress — then he violates the STOCK Act, trades stock in the industries he claims to fight, and votes against the very ban he claims to be fighting for,”_**Conroy said.**_“Today he even voted against requiring an ID to vote, something every Ohioan already does without a problem. Washington politicians like Greg Landsman serve the special interests and enrich themselves. I'm running to serve the people of the First District, and no one else.”_ Voters in Ohio's First District will have a clear choice in November: a career politician who says one thing and does another, or a career public servant who has spent his life defending this country.**###**

I'm running to serve the people of the First District, and no one else.” Voters in Ohio's First District will have a clear choice in November: a career politician who says one thing and does another, or a career public servant who has spent his life defending this country.### | | | | | | | | | | Conroy for Congress 2692 Madison Rd Ste N1 Box #358 Cincinnati, OH 45208-1320 USA or |

subject: Save the date!
body:
---
| |
---
|

| VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS!
---
|
---
| It's been a great week in the district![Orange County Public Schools ](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/63P_Bddob/c?w=5PAr-FkA43JegDFhieR6WTeRt5QPkhj0oE8JhIPTEgI.)broke ground on the long awaited CTE site that will be a blessing for generations of students in Orange County! I want to commend the Board of Supervisors, the School Board, and Dr. Hornick for their many efforts in bringing this to fruition. I, along with Delegate [Phillip Scott](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/63P_Bddob/c?w=I743tZFTrVuMcEFdZqo-MEg_SffXQoN40gAouf6zpQc.), also had a highly informative meeting with Jason C. Smith, [Orange County Sheriff](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/63P_Bddob/c?w=Dbu1p7TtMkTCsreOcWuBfzqbpmRU83oz9JxTw_hA518.) to hear how the recent new laws are impacting them and find out how we can help them continue to be successful in their duties. They are doing an incredible job keeping crime rates low and I am grateful for their service, professionalism and dedication to Orange County.
---
| | [](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/63P_Bddob/c?w=zRfqL4LWeTFMWnK4dVSnyahsSYPlJ9txxg6j10eAsvw.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGFtaWx0b25mb3J2aXJnaW5pYS5jb20vbWVldC1rYXJlbiIsInIiOiIiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiI0NDI4ODkzMy1lNGNjLTRmMTItOGYzZS02ZjQ1ZjM3NjIxZjQifQ)
---
---
---
---
| I was also excited to attend a ribbon cutting at [Prince Michel Vineyard & Winery](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/63P_Bddob/c?w=2zyczloXgL9HfSGhvnEUm8D2f5Lm2bAduFDLBNPO3n0.) of Madison County to celebrate their spectacular new barrel and wine tasting room! Virginia's wine industry contributes between $1.5 to 5 billion each year to Virginia's economy, but they were hit with a devastating late freeze this year. In MAGA’s America, hate is on the rise.
I need to tell you about something that happened in Frisco, Texas — and why I refuse to stay quiet about it.
At a protest outside Frisco City Hall, a demonstrator tore an Indian flag to pieces while the crowd chanted bigoted slurs. Not political disagreement. Hate — the kind of raw, targeted intimidation designed to make entire communities feel like they don't belong here.
I've seen where that leads. I'm an immigrant. I've had a sitting elected official publicly call for the mass deportation of Indians and label me a "foreign occupier."
That's exactly the kind of hate Equal Opportunity Now was built to fight — will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help us elect leaders who will never stay silent in the face of it? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
DONATE TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Here's the thing about hate like this: it starts small. A torn flag. A chant. And if leaders look away and hope it passes, it never stops there.
Meanwhile, hate in all its forms is skyrocketing.
I joined a coalition of Members of Congress to condemn what happened in Frisco in the strongest possible terms — because every community targeted by hate deserves leaders who will stand up and say clearly: this has no place in our country.
But condemning hate isn't enough. We have to out-organize it, out-fight it, and elect more leaders who will never flinch in the face of it.
That's why I founded Equal Opportunity Now — to support the leaders who will stand up for immigrant communities, for South Asian families, for every American being told they don't belong.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect them? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?refcode=260722_eon_frisco&amount=25]
CHIP IN TODAY, THERE'S NO TIME TO WASTE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
They can tear a flag. They can shout their hatred in the street. But they will not make us afraid, and they will not make us stop.
Immigrants belong here. And we're not going to stop fighting against hate.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

body:
[image: image.png]

Team Helena Campaign Update

Every day I hear people across Rhode Island say they are ready for change,
and the excitement about Helena continues to grow in every community across
our state. With the primary election less than 50 days away, we need to do
everything we can to ensure Helena becomes the next governor of Rhode
Island.

One of the best ways to support the campaign is by volunteering at one of
our upcoming events. Please see the list below for upcoming volunteer
opportunities, and stay tuned for next week's edition where we will
officially launch our canvassing campaign!

With gratitude,
Elisabeth Wales, Volunteer Director, Helena for Rhode Island

Volunteer Opportunities and Ways to Support Helena!

-

Saturday, July 25, all day (Pawtucket): Come table for Helena at
the Colombian
Independence Festival. There will be live music, a variety of
Latin-American food and refreshments, handcrafts, and more! Helena's team
will have a designated table during the event. Register to volunteer by
clicking here.
<https://helenafoulkes-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/2aJXj2SJpG28vYjl31Zw5j51Fj6hwBbA5iZQfrYO8Kg3FwAGRnwEQw2apG2khBMigd_NJa6Tz44fNt1fDzEFuH_0iGVKnQ4rf65UIOrgPeDcc8QjyJU6evhKeGn8Ua8J5NMNbJ6lQkd5mL5WA0txTvUbMpFcUtWARDcEI6A7VR121Cki9eGM8TbCPCI_qytnTd84CmA>

-

Sunday, July 26, 12:00PM-2:00PM (Providence): Spread the word about
Helena at the Liberian Independence Day Festival! Helena volunteers will
enjoy the festival and pass out information about Helena to the attendees.
Helena will be attending, and we're looking for volunteers to support her
at this event! You can register at this link: Join Helena at the
Liberian Independence Day Festival.
<https://helenafoulkes-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/2T2emKLqpcpyWXLk9wlRjO0OA8xsvCL-jIhl7tZqmLqLJwAGRnwEI5b-CZJdH5i0lrpd15yIm4l_NkCcUNyP52UH-4ak1ZqmaolZBDGoI0nRZBcFvESWWxwWdnMXlSnj4hHt_yJaN0nZi3C-9OGOuILGjx9XF3S-3S8yxWOv3iInvykL9VXhSAu3nA4oHiDZukuBUAkuxSJ737TRxXX6_BN7P4J_k-Vs3feLV15iM9crmMvIRv9lF9AgullnqQZMs5rBAET5G-MC5k2dWP1ZDiOnz03Z24Ek6xDfvwwK4Zne0cRO3>

Share why you are supporting Helena by clicking this link

Need inspiration? Read Sonia’s reflection below! P.S. Thank you so much
to those who submitted responses last week!

Volunteer Spotlight: Sonia Pensa

[image: image.png]

“Why Helena?” Story Series

My name is Sonia Pensa, and I'm a rising sophomore at Georgetown University
studying government and mathematics. My Rhode Island roots are strong: I
grew up in the East Greenwich School system, passed my driver's test at the
Cranston DMV, and recently voted in my first election at Providence City
Hall! I see this internship as a way to give back to the state that I love
and that has given so much to me. Not only does it provide invaluable
experience in civic work, but I make a tangible impact on my local
community alongside a fantastic team of dedicated and supportive interns.
Their enthusiasm is contagious. Whether through collecting signatures,
cheering on Helena at local events, or dropping off yard signs and bumper
stickers in every corner of Rhode Island, I've found each aspect of this
experience to be profoundly rewarding.

I also wholeheartedly believe in Helena's mission and truly think our state
will thrive under her leadership. With two healthcare-worker parents,
Helena's plans to improve our hospital system and support healthcare
providers particularly speak to me – and after spending the summer on this
team, I have complete faith in the follow-through on these plans. Helena
and her team are so committed to this state and its constituents, and I'm
beyond proud to be involved in this campaign.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Heroes in American Conservation: Aldo Leopold, the Ethical Ecologist
body:
Meet American Conservation Hero Aldo Leopold!
Meet American Conservation Hero Aldo Leopold!
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795900/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795901/38SyG9Xl)
---
#
Meet American Conservation Hero Aldo Leopold
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Who is she?_**
Nicknamed the “Ethical Ecologist,” Aldo Leopold (1887–1948) is considered the father of modern wildlife management. In fact, we still use many of his methods today. Leopold was guided by a philosophy he called the “Land Ethic” — the idea that humans have a moral obligation to one other and to nature, which has intrinsic value of its own. You can learn more in his groundbreaking book of essays, _A Sand County Almanac_.
#
He worked for the U.S. Forest Service (1909-1928) in the Southwest region and helped establish the first official wilderness area, [**Gila National Forest wilderness.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795902/38SyG9Xl) He then went on to teach wildlife management at the University of Wisconsin.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Why is Leopold called the founder of wildlife management?_**
As a hunter, Leopold witnessed how removing apex predators can devastate an ecosystem. He was among the first scientists to recognize the far-reaching consequences of [**removing animals like wolves**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795903/38SyG9Xl) , and he advocated for the protection of predators and sustainable hunting practices.
#
He also stressed the importance of habitat preservation to support and protect all wildlife. When sandhill cranes were on the brink of extinction with just 20 estimated pairs remaining, Leopold championed wetland preservation to help these birds recover.
#
Leopold’s work highlights the importance of saving all pieces of an ecosystem: predators, prey and habitat. This was a foundation for modern conservation efforts as well as the U.S. Endangered Species Act.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can you become a conservation hero?_**
Leopold’s Land Ethic idea came at a time when advancing technology was pulling people away from nature, like it is today. We see this disconnect in our modern world, as many legislators and even some Members of Congress are [**trying to dismantle the ESA**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795904/38SyG9Xl) and other conservation efforts. [**Defenders of Wildlife**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5795905/38SyG9Xl) works to respond to new conservation threats and to develop solutions that improve outcomes for wildlife. You can help by speaking out in your community and to your leaders to protect our most imperiled wildlife and their homes!
#
|
---
###
_A note on our Heroes in American Conservation series: Our country has a long and complex history, populated with high-profile figures whose views may have been complicated or divisive in their time as well as ours. We present these conservationists in the interest of creating a greater understanding of the roots of the American conservation movement, and to inspire you to make your own contribution to ongoing conversations about how we preserve our wild world._
#
---
| | |
---
