QUITO, Ecuador--Alexandra Bravo, the prosecutor assigned to investigate U.S. strikes on three Ecuadorian boats and the 36 survivors' subsequent accounts of torture and kidnapping, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta last month. According to police, on June 14 a hitman aboard a black motorcycle opened fire on Bravo as she and her sister were leaving a cafe at about 11 a.m. Bravo's sister, who jumped to protect her, was also killed in the attack. Upon arriving at the crime scene, officers say they found five 9mm shell casings and Bravo's injured driver, but no sign of the police detail that had been assigned to protect her. The Police Directorate, which operates entirely under the executive branch, has launched a probe to determine if there'd been an internal security breach. Bravo is the 26th member of Ecuador's justice system to be assassinated since 2020 and the . Besides her usual caseload of homicide and organized crime, Bravo had been working the Fiorella, Negra Francisca, and Don Maca cases--. Two of the boat's crews returned home and reported being abducted, blindfolded, and starved for eight days by American gunmen in U.S. military uniforms aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol ship, before being abandoned in El Salvador. The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances endorsed the calls for an investigation, demanding that the U.S. provide information on the whereabouts of the eight still-missing men and any involvement in the matter by April 27. To date, the United States has not responded. Under Ecuador's right-wing president Daniel Noboa-- country has become a central testing ground for Operation Southern Spear, Washington's extrajudicial bombing campaign purporting to target "narco-terrorists," which has killed 221 people to date. There is no evidence that many of the victims, including those in Bravo's investigation, had engaged in drug trafficking. "I can't make any assertion regarding it being a political assassination, but evidently, when a prosecutor is killed it's because of the investigation they're conducting," Fernando Bastias, a renowned human rights attorney with Ecuador's CDH and member of the Geneva-based World Organization Against Torture, told Drop Site, "That's something we've learned from our experience in Ecuador." A source inside the Manta police department, who knew Bravo personally, told Drop Site that the Ecuadorian prosecutor was under pressure from her superiors at the Attorney General's office to treat the U.S. attacks as exclusively "cases of disappearance." The source, who asked for anonymity out of fear of retaliation, said Bravo was told to close all lines of inquiry after 36 of the 44 missing men were found--despite arriving with severe injuries, including 70% vision loss and feet torn to flesh and bone, which medical experts found consistent with their accounts of explosions and torture. A senior researcher with Human Rights Watch, Nathalye Cotrino Villarreal, who interviewed Bravo as part of her investigation into the three vessels, similarly recalled Bravo facing "internal challenges within the institution itself to advance the investigation." Villarreal said the prosecutor repeatedly sought cooperation from other branches responsible for the ship's rescue, including the Manta Port Captaincy, but "none responded to her requests for information." During the Negra Francisca bombing, Darwin Pico-Flores, an eyewitness aboard a nearby boat, told Drop Site he called the Manta Port Captaincy to request emergency assistance. Nobody came. In April, as part of its first investigation into the incident, Drop Site called the port seeking comment. Officials hung up after learning the call was from journalists. As of their last meeting on May 8, Cotrino Villarreal told Drop Site, Bravo "was still in the initial stages of inquiry and investigation." Bastias said Bravo "was investigating a country [United States] that has been positioned in the media as an ally against crime. That investigation has not advanced at all, and that stems from an intention to avoid getting into trouble or problems with anyone." The source inside the Manta Police Department said that, given this lack of cooperation from partner agencies, Bravo had asked for advice on how to pursue new sources for evidence. In the days leading up to her death, Bravo was relocated to the Attorney General's office in Montecristi, a neighboring municipality. Her caseload changed after the transfer and she was no longer in charge of investigating the three boat attacks. Drop Site attempted to reach Bravo's replacement for comment but he had been explicitly instructed not to speak to the press. After weeks of attempts to reach the Attorney General's office for comment, they told Drop Site the investigation was sealed and they could not comment on why Bravo was relocated. Inside Ecuador's U.S.-backed military regime,. "It's already a major obstacle for prosecutors to investigate local state agents. Now imagine international state agents," Bastias said. "The Executive Branch has implemented a series of legal frameworks that leave these foreign state agents immune from prosecution," he added, referring to the diplomatic immunity granted to all U.S. military and Department of Defense personnel through President Noboa's 22 martial law decrees. The Pentagon, Coast Guard, and U.S. Southern Command have all denied any knowledge or responsibility of the boat incidents. After Drop Site published photo evidence of the Negra Francisca bombing, U.S. . On June 13, the day before Bravo's murder, Reps. Joaquin Castro (D-Texas) and Bill Keating (D-Mass.) Hegseth, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Head of the U.S. Coast Guard, Kevin Lunday, Despite the deadline of July 10, none of the agencies have issued a public response. Keating's press secretary Lauren McDermott told Drop Site that his office had received a reply from Rubio's office, but none from the Department of War or Coast Guard. She did not disclose the contents of the response. The survivors who returned home, and the families of those who didn't, still have not received any answers, telling Drop Site "authorities shut the door in our face." Maria, the wife of one of the fishermen, tells Drop Site her mother-in-law died awaiting her son's return, saying she was struggling with severe depression and stopped in the weeks leading up to her death. Despite both governments' efforts to stonewall the investigation, evidence continues to emerge supporting the fishermen's accounts of abduction, airstrikes, and torture. Drop Site obtained exclusive video of U.S. Coast Guard activity in the vicinity of the Negra Francisca bombing, open-source intelligence that corroborates the Negra Francisca's testimonies, and police interviews with eyewitnesses that confirm the U.S. involvement alleged by survivors and documented by Drop Site. With the help of Airwars OSINT analyst and former U.S. Marine Corps member Tomi McCluskey, Drop Site accessed additional NASA thermal imagery consistent with the Negra Francisca bombing and vessel tracking data placing U.S. Coast Guard activity along the route the fishermen say they were taken after the strike. Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike. Political Lawfare Under Ecuador 's U.S.-Backed Military Regime Noboa, who governs by military curfews and , has gone to great lengths to become Trump's strongest partner in South America. Since taking office, he brushed aside Ecuador's constitutional ban on U.S. military presence--ratified by 60% of voters as recently as November 2025--which was originally introduced precisely due to a history of U.S. military sinking boats off the coast of Manta. Additionally, his administration authorized the first FBI office on Ecuadorian soil, assisted a to falsely frame members of Colombia's left-wing government ahead of elections, and collaborated with the U.S. in of innocent civilian farmworkers along the Colombian-Ecuadorian border--all in the name of combatting drug trafficking. Notably, boats from Noboa's were caught trafficking ₤26 million of cocaine--a detail that has not deterred the State Department from naming him a key partner in Trump's War on Drugs. Last month, The Guardian that a whistleblower who was investigating Noboa's ties to drug trafficking was murdered. Still, Noboa remains a member in good standing of Trump's Shield of the Americas. The Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, as the Shield is also known, functions as both a military and a highly political alliance, having openly intervened to prop up U.S. interests in Bolivia as President Rodrigo Paz faced off with anti-austery protests. A local prosecutor charging U.S. forces with extrajudicial bombings and torture of Ecuadorian civilians would undermine the alliance and damage Ecuador-U.S. relations. Other government officials investigating U.S.-Ecuadorian criminal collusion received death threats. Monica Palacios, a National Assembly lawmaker representing Ecuadorians living in the United States, who announced plans to bring the Fiorella boat case before the United Nations, faced months of political lawfare after exposing a U.S.-Ecuadorian government embezzlement scandal. Last Friday, against herself and her one-year-old son, along with footage of the outside of her New York home. She directly blamed President Noboa, saying the threats were retaliation for her investigation into U.S.-Ecuadorian corruption. "There is a direct persecution of judges and prosecutors who, within the scope of their duties, make decisions that are not entirely aligned with what the Executive Branch wants and end up being sanctioned," Bastias, the human rights attorney, said. "On the other hand, there is also the risk stemming from the context of criminality." Regardless, he asserted, Bravo's death "has a lot to do with what the state does or does not do, because so far there haven't been any effective security mechanisms for the justice system's civil servants. The responsibility lies in having failed to ensure protection." | | ---|---|--- Alexandra Bravo, prosecutor for Ecuador 's Attorney General's Office, during an interview with Radio San Mateo. Photo provided to Drop Site News by Radio San Mateo. Diego Vintimilla Jarrin, formerly a lawmaker with Ecuador's National Assembly and now a spokesperson for Ecuador's Communist Party, similarly told Drop Site, "Noboa's government is the most anti-sovereign agenda we have had since the start of democracy. I have no proof of who murdered the prosecutor but the fact that she was investigating certain elements and that they later ceased to seem important also says a lot about the underlying issues." New Evidence Implicating U.S. Emerges The Negra Francisca The U.S. maintains it never interacted with any of the three boats. A spokesperson for the U.S. Coast Guard told The Guardian that the agency's only involvement in the events was deploying the USCGC Bertholf on a search-and-rescue mission after receiving a MAYDAY alert that the Negra Francisca was on fire, and ultimately found nothing. But tracking data of the Bertholf's movements, provided exclusively to Drop Site by McCluskey, places the cutter near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing before turning off its signal--only to reappear off the shore of Costa Rica the same dates the Negra Francisca crew were taken into Central American waters and transferred to El Salvador's Naval Command, with mangled limbs and major burn injuries from the attack. Hernan Flores, captain of the Negra Francisca, told Drop Site that Salvadoran officers specifically informed him that "U.S. personnel had called to coordinate the handoff." The Coast Guard denied that it coordinated the handoff. "The Coast Guard did not play any role in the transfer of fishermen from the Negra Francisca Duarte II," said a spokesperson. | | ---|---|--- The USCGC Bertholf operating in Costa Rican waters on the same dates (times converted from UTC) that the Negra Francisca crew members were brought to Central America and received by El Salvador 's Navy/Coast Guard. Photo from Global Fishing Watch, provided by OSINT analyst Tomi McCluskey. The USCGC Bertholf departed the Galapagos military base at 4 p.m. on March 16 and stopped transmitting its location shortly afterwards. A day later, the Negra Francisca was bombed 170 miles away--a distance typically covered by boat in 3 to 10 hours. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard to account for the cutter's activity after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded it "does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security." At 1:02 p.m. on March 17, NASA FIRMS registered a thermal anomaly consistent with an explosive fire, corroborating the time and location where Negra Francisca fishermen told Drop Site their ship was set ablaze by multi-drone strikes. The crew say they were then seized at gunpoint by English-speaking men with blond hair dressed in khaki fatigues with American flag patches stitched onto their sleeves--their descriptions match the uniforms pictured in . Aboard the U.S.-flagged patrol ship, the gunmen allegedly held them hostage, sank their bombed boat, placed hoods over their heads, beat some of the fishermen, and withheld food for eight days as they transported them to Central America. | | ---|---|--- OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey document the USCGC Bertholf 's movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC). | | ---|---|--- OSINT provided to Drop Site by Tomi McCluskey documenting the USCGC Bertholf 's movements near the Negra Francisca around the time of the bombing (times converted from UTC). The USCGC Bertholf's signal resurfaced in Costa Rican waters on March 22 near the Golfito Port, approximately 450 nautical miles from El Salvador's waters. It turned off its transponder and did not reactivate it until March 24, 24 hours after El Salvador's Coast Guard publicly announced having had the Negra Francisca fishermen in their custody. As part of our first investigation, Drop Site reached out to 11 government personnel in El Salvador. All of them refused to go on the record, citing a media gag order. There is precedent for the Bertholf transferring victims of U.S. airstrikes to Central American authorities, with Costa Rican outlets reporting it delivered the remains of two deceased and one injured survivor to Costa Rica's Port of Golfito around the same time. Costa Rica's nautical inspector Wilber Urroz Guido said he had no information on the cutter's movements but that it was authorized to act under a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Costa Rica--similar to agreements the U.S. maintains with Ecuador and El Salvador. Eyewitness testimony also casts doubt on the U.S. Coast Guard's version of events. Video footage shared exclusively with Drop Site by Darwin Flores-Pico, an eyewitness to the attack and nephew of the Negra Francisca's captain, shows a U.S. Coast Guard cutter patrolling the waters where the bombing occurred. Video obtained by Drop Site showing alleged Coast Guard activity near the Negra Francisca strike. Darwin said he was fishing nearby on March 17, aboard his boat the Solavil, when he spotted smoke rising in the distance around 2 p.m. While making repeated attempts to reach the Negra Francisca's crew by radio, he spotted an American aircraft circling above. It wasn't until hours later that he learned by radio signal that the Negra Francisca was in flames and rushed to make his way to the scene, finding the vessel consumed by fire and no sign of survivors. He recovered two scorched emergency skiffs, took photo evidence of the fire, then called the Port of Manta to ask for help. Nobody came. Darwin decided to begin his journey back to the port to get emergency assistance and, as he was leaving the scene of the fire, red and green lights descended upon the Negra Francisca. Fearing for his safety, he steered his boat away from the site. | | ---|---|--- The Negra Francisca burning, photographed and shared with Drop Site by Darwin Pico-Flores. The following afternoon, Darwin told Drop Site his boat was boarded by the U.S. Coast Guard, which detained and questioned the crew for nearly 12 hours via a Spanish translator with a Puerto Rican accent. He said Coast Guard personnel confirmed the red and green lights were from their patrol and acknowledged reaching the site of the Negra Francisca the previous night, but refused to elaborate on anything they'd found. Instead, they questioned the fishermen about whether they'd seen anything and why Darwin had salvaged the skiffs. After telling the Coast Guard officials that the Negra Francisca was his uncle's boat, Darwin says they abruptly stopped questioning him and began communicating by radio in English with colleagues aboard the nearby cutter shown in the video. "Since we were the only people who saw everything, we were afraid they might do something to us," Darwin said. He felt the U.S. Coast Guard showed little interest in helping him locate his family and instead seemed more focused on "making sure we weren't witnesses to anything." McCluskey says the multi-drone tactic--described by all three boats--reflects a U.S. doctrine. He argues it's unlikely that other regional powers, from neighboring countries to organized crime groups, would have the budget or access for such technology. There is no known precedent of cartels using "eye-in-the-sky" surveillance drones deep in maritime territory, though the Coast Guard has also denied operating armed drones in Ecuadorian waters. Furthermore, the decision to keep the survivors alive, albeit involving testimonies of torture, and the efforts and expenses to transport them, is far more reflective of a Department of Defense protocol---designed to avoid international legal ramifications--than any organized crime group would typically care to practice. "If it was cartels, you would've never found them," McCluskey said. "There would be no survivors to talk to, there would be no stories." The Fiorella The Fiorella was struck off the coast of the Galapagos on January 20; all eight fishermen aboard remain missing. The day before the vessel vanished, the captain's wife received a call from her husband on an emergency line, warning that U.S. aircraft were orbiting overhead. Drop Site obtained police interview transcripts from two eyewitnesses, Christian Flores and Dimas Ignacio Álvarez, who corroborated seeing the Fiorella engulfed in smoke and surrounded by American assets. The two men were members of the Fiorella crew but had been out setting a long line on a nearby raft for several hours when the vessel went up in smoke. In their police statements, Flores and Álvarez described two U.S. aircraft flying over the Fiorella on January 18; multiple grey American drones and a U.S.-flagged patrol ship circling the vessel on January 19; and, on January 20--the day their crewmates disappeared--the large U.S.-flagged patrol ship near the smoke. From a distance, they could not make out the personnel aboard the ship, but their accounts echo those of the Negra Francisca crew, who said they were taken hostage by armed Americans aboard a U.S.-flagged patrol vessel. The witnesses' descriptions also match aircraft and equipment featured in public posts by U.S. Southern Command. Transcripts of police interviews with the eyewitnesses, obtained exclusively by Drop Site News. Originals in Spanish, translated copies in English. After spotting the smoke, the two fishermen said they heard their crewmates calling the captain over the radio in distress. They were never seen again. The attorney representing the two survivors of the Fiorella, Juan Avila, told Drop Site that the slain prosecutor, Alexandra Bravo, was in fact his niece. The Coast Guard told Drop Site it "has no record of involvement with La Fiorella." Bravo Is No Anomaly The absence of an assigned police detail when Bravo was murdered bears similarities to the 2023 assassination of frontrunner presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio. A congressional commission determined that Villavicencio's police detail was insufficient, that he had been unconventionally escorted through an exposed street-level exit contrary to standard protocol, and that the armored vehicle designated to protect Villavicencio on the campaign trail had been left by his security team in another city that day. These breaches made him particularly vulnerable when assailants approached and shot him on the sidewalk as he was leaving a meeting with other government officials. Villavicencio's death cleared the way for now-President Daniel Noboa's campaign-- surge to victory. In an interview with Señal Colombia, National Assembly legislator and member of Villavicencio's party, Gisella Molina, who was with him and injured during the assassination, suggested government officials had prior knowledge of the plot. During the 2024 murder investigation, Drop Site private messages from then-Attorney General Diana Salazar revealing a plot to implicate former democratic socialist President Correa's party in Villavicencio's assassination, amid close collaboration with the U.S. ambassador. The state later concluded that the Los Lobos cartel carried out Villavicencio's murder and alleged that former members of Correa's party were the masterminds. Prosecutors assert that Los Lobos killed Villavicencio for exposing their criminal network. While Villavicencio campaigned on eradicating the cartel economy, Ecuador under Noboa-- risen as the top distribution hub for 70% of the world's cocaine. Immediately following Bravo's death, the Attorney General issued a public statement attributing her murder to retaliation against prosecutors combating organized crime. When asked why authorities had linked the killing to organized crime and whether investigators had uncovered any information about Bravo's missing police protection detail, the Attorney General's office told Drop Site the investigation is under seal and declined to comment. Though the attorney general has yet to present evidence to support their claim, Bravo lamented to the Human Rights Watch that "danger was always present" in her work. "She said that being a prosecutor in a context of organized crime was complex and risky, but she did not provide any further details," Cotrino Villarreal told Drop Site. Manta sits at the epicenter of Ecuador's organized crime crisis, as the small South American country becomes in the Western Hemisphere. Bravo was also responsible for looking into the unsolved 2024 disappearance of the Patricia Lynn ship and its 21 crew members. Bravo is the second person associated with the Patricia Lynn case to be assassinated. The first was the mother-in-law of one of the disappeared fishermen who became the spokesperson for the victims' families and organized marches demanding answers for their missing relatives. Maria Choez was fatally shot by two armed assailants while operating her street food stand in downtown Manta. Cotrino Villarreal says the sinking of the Ecuadorian waters, "served as a precedent in all these ship-related matters." "If Ecuador had a framework of trust in its institutions, one might think [Bravo's murder] was an ordinary crime," Vintimilla Jarrin, the former lawmaker, said. "But given the systematic violence against judges, prosecutors, and lawyers, there isn't much room to give them the benefit of the doubt. clean_body: Every contribution today helps reach voters before this critical primary. | Friends, it's Jane. In all my years of activism, I've learned that real leaders don't wait for a title to start fighting. Justin Pearson is one of those leaders, and today, JanePAC is proud to endorse him for Congress in Tennessee's 9th District. = = | = Justin's story is exactly why I started this PAC. During the pandemic, Big Oil tried to build a crude oil pipeline through frontline communities in South Memphis. Justin co-founded a community group, organized his neighbors, and won. The pipeline was canceled. Then he helped lead the fight to shut down a facility that had been releasing toxic chemicals into Memphis's air for half a century. Today, he's taking on Elon Musk himself — fighting a hyperscale data center just across the state line that's polluting South Memphis while burning through unpermitted gas turbines. And in the Tennessee legislature, he's carried that same courage into office: protecting clean water, demanding transparency from polluters, and standing up to the fossil fuel industry, even when it made him a target. But I have to be honest with you about what Justin is up against. After the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, Tennessee Republicans rushed to redraw his district — slicing up Memphis and stretching TN-09 into deep-red territory to try to erase a majority-minority district that has had a voice in Congress for decades. Civil rights groups are suing to stop the maps. The Democratic incumbent retired. And Republicans are betting that we'll simply give up. But Justin isn't backing down. He's made it clear that no matter what map Tennessee ends up using, he's still running unbroken and undeterred. I believe him. body:

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/DYHkdM5cJDh?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Hi Peter,
For years, Josh Shapiro has carefully cultivated an image as a governor who can appeal to everyone.
But after nearly four years in office, one question keeps getting harder to answer:
**Who is Josh Shapiro actually fighting for?**

A [**piece published last week**](https://us.list-manage.com/l1Lh3idEoaq?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd) in RealClearPennsylvania argues that despite all the attention surrounding Josh Shapiro, he has failed to build a lasting constituency because his positions often change depending on the audience. The piece argues that while his political ambitions continue to grow, his record has left many Pennsylvanians wondering what he truly stands for.
Think about it.
He promised parents more educational opportunities, then walked away from school choice.
He talks about supporting Pennsylvania’s energy workers while pushing policies that create uncertainty for one of our most important industries.
He claims to be focused on Pennsylvania, yet seems far more interested in building a national political brand than solving the challenges facing families here at home.
**Pennsylvania doesn’t need another politician focused on the next office.**
**Pennsylvania needs a governor focused on this one.**

That's why Stacy Garrity has spent this campaign meeting directly with farmers worried about losing their land, veterans who deserve better care, parents who want more opportunities for their children, law enforcement officers keeping our communities safe, and families struggling with the rising cost of living.
While Josh Shapiro focuses on headlines, Stacy Garrity is focused on Pennsylvanians.
That's the difference this election is all about.
Thank you for standing with us.
\- Team Garrity

Those recent Supreme Court decisions include curtailing abortion rights by overturning Roe v. Wade and the ruling in Louisiana v. Callais that significantly weakened a key section of the Voting Rights Act.

Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Peter.

But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. **[However, I cannot do this alone.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=2d6368b380474b21b906895b6b8b2e91&_e=a5ElJvGj1ptfQKGnwSCwQLTZhbhN4gcGleSKJR4rjrgH7Rkq9j8c43zK5c95PommD_ZA4vXoZUu1eEGUv04kOoSDkPRCzeirSZ3oe_CgBJa4SopmTw1y6QnxBTBIeL8prshTWMxM9nV9U40RLMLMHOxrSDfDnH92BW0TCfujNpfl8DVue1UG9Nld1-GCOcuJDOnUrzGnmFD-jLSMUAaid5DTwWcWfXtCHIYHkhN8nPsnzNPlZRTDGxONAdY6BPq52bVl-qVcmiapIHZo0VM4J3OJrxrqzX6_oS4fh9UtNwJW5AE2gAtQ8RC6P-Erv7tr1WcetZvE3lp-dv88jrzIoXfRowmRiBIWSbGFkgzYUC47_5YypfOfYBF1C0NSK2ztAvkxhTYhJQEJ7YdhpdlAsMvg6LysbGBoxfPWalvt6zsxjZYax6RDI1nvKVrIc2671HVn95XeaKXRYE99WuBkTyKNETvZWejPnq2uXrRN-jcdvWeULKLeRo7QqdCY-8JGFf6_GYgm--faQJoCgIcZsLxKUkQdEzQmQ1GqRpa-HjYZldMAJUUJnKPJuHUVnmqaUVJHb_7XO3rsJCIjTBrDcadf8Tk7-kc_nhdWzb4pDiveDfkWemq_g1PsbpT1otAeIeE4654NxVkbT7jCk7X2TNDy_PuMdmM3gZ9Gvrv_r02uJfFzsF00kLYWoFwrdIOt019tPBgppN7So1wvwP1LFABBUBIfRMx0Cli-dhu_cqiBPH0OhcoG8RCyUt7QLjH5)**

clean_body: I'm ready for the fight ahead, and I'm all in to run for the United States Senate. | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. I never thought I'd be in this position, but I am ready to answer the call from President Trump. I am ready to run. | | Paid for by Darline for Senate Don't want to receive any more of our emails? Trump has installed cronies
across the federal judiciary, all the way up to the Supreme Court.

These aren't just loyalists protecting Trump's abuses of power. They're
not just shielding his billionaire backers from accountability. They're
actively dismantling our fundamental freedoms and rights in courtrooms
across the country.

Take a look at just some of what his judges have done:

* Reproductive rights: Tried to block patients from getting
mifepristone through the mail.
* Workers and economic security: Sided against workers owed overtime.
Blocked a veteran from getting the disability benefits they earned.
Undid an order that protected a union's right to bargain.
* Immigration: Denied an immigrant a fair shot at relief when they
couldn't get proper translation help. Greenlit a deportation without
ever reviewing the immigrant's own testimony in person. Opened the
door to fast-tracked deportations nationwide with no hearing at all.
* Voting rights: Gutted voting rights protections. Allowed
gerrymandered maps that weaken the power of voters of color.

These judges are literally working Trump’s extremist agenda into our lives
rather than upholding the Constitution or protecting the American people.

And Trump isn’t done. This term alone, he’s nominated 60 judges. 51 have
already been confirmed, with more to come.

We cannot let more of his political puppets take lifetime seats on the
bench just to erode our freedoms and democracy one ruling at a time.

Demand Justice PAC is fighting back. We're calling Trump and his corrupt
administration out. We're exposing these crony nominees and their records.
We're mobilizing nationwide pressure to stop these confirmations.

Throughout my career, I worked alongside people who believed that public service meant doing the right thing—even when it wasn't easy. That belief is what led me to run for Congress. Over the past several months, I've traveled across Southwestern Pennsylvania holding town halls and meeting with people in every corner of our district. Whether I'm talking with retirees worried about Social Security, parents concerned about rising costs, veterans, small business owners, or young families trying to get ahead, I hear the same message: people want honest leadership that focuses on solving problems instead of creating them. I agree. That's why I'm running on a simple promise: to bring integrity, accountability, and common-sense leadership to Congress. I'll work to protect Social Security and Medicare, create more economic opportunity for working families, support our veterans, and restore trust in our government by putting people ahead of politics. But campaigns like ours don't rely on corporate PACs or special interests. We rely on people who believe we can do better. clean_body: We need integrity, accountability, and common-sense leadership in Congress | Friends, When I graduated from Washington & Jefferson College, I chose a life of service. I served as an Army helicopter pilot during Desert Storm, then spent twenty years as an FBI Special Agent investigating crime, corruption, and terrorism. Throughout my career, I worked alongside people who believed that public service meant doing the right thing—even when it wasn't easy. That belief is what led me to run for Congress. Over the past several months, I've traveled across Southwestern Pennsylvania holding town halls and meeting with people in every corner of our district. Whether I'm talking with retirees worried about Social Security, parents concerned about rising costs, veterans, small business owners, or young families trying to get ahead, I hear the same message: people want honest leadership that focuses on solving problems instead of creating them. I agree. That's why I'm running on a simple promise: to bring integrity, accountability, and common-sense leadership to Congress. I'll work to protect Social Security and Medicare, create more economic opportunity for working families, support our veterans, and restore trust in our government by putting people ahead of politics. But campaigns like ours don't rely on corporate PACs or special interests. We rely on people who believe we can do better. If you've saved your payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately. Every contribution helps us hold more town halls, knock on more doors, make more phone calls, and share our message with voters throughout the district. Thank you for believing in this campaign and for everything you're doing to help us build a better future. Sincerely, Alan Bradstock MAGA loyalist Guy Reschenthaler has consistently put party loyalty and corporate interests ahead of working families in our district. It’s time for real leadership that puts people first. Democrat Alan Bradstock is stepping up to fight for affordable healthcare, reproductive freedom, workers’ rights, and a stronger democracy, but he can’t do it without your support. Peter,
Growing up in Dallas, I watched my mom serve on the Dallas school board and fight for public education. She showed me that public service means standing up for your community, doing the hard work, and refusing to back down when people are counting on you.
I've dedicated my life to serving Texans. During my four terms in the Texas House, I’ve fought for our teachers and neighborhood schools, affordable healthcare, reproductive freedom, higher wages, clean water, and good-paying jobs.
Now, I believe Texans deserve a serious, hard-working, steady-handed leader in the Senate.
That's why I am running: to make sure every Texan has access to affordable healthcare, a great public education, clean water, and a good-paying job that allows them to build a better future.
But I can't do it alone.
Peter, this campaign is about building a better future for all of us. Will you join me and help bring real change to Texas? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/Goodwin-email?refcode=20260723_em_fr_b1_VG_engaged]

Throughout her life, Vikki has strived to build a better Texas for her family, her clients and her constituents. Now, she has her sights set on returning sanity to Texas government and restoring a collaborative and cooperative spirit, putting aside things that divide us, with a focus on real issues, not distractions.
Representative Vikki Goodwin is serving her fourth term in the Texas Legislature, representing parts of Austin and the Lake Travis area, and she is currently running for Lt. Governor of Texas. She is a passionate supporter of Texas public schools, has steadfastly voted against vouchers, and will continue to do so.
As a member of the Appropriations Article III Subcommittee overseeing education funding, she champions educational equity and access at all levels. Her priorities are to increase funding to public schools, housing affordability, water infrastructure, and access to healthcare.
Now, she's running for Lt. Governor against Dan Patrick to build a collaborative and cooperative spirit, putting aside things that divide us and focusing on real issues that impact real Texans.

body:
The next generation of organizers is training right now — take a look inside. | | | Peter, Right now — as you read this — 15 immigrant youth leaders from across the country are in the middle of a six-week intensive training called **Level Up: The Dream Lab.** They're from across the country: California, the D.C. area, New York, Illinois, Florida, Ohio, Texas, and Kansas. Twelve sessions across six weeks. And by the end, every single one of them will lead their own community event. **[Will you chip in $10 to power the leadership development and movement-building work that makes programs like the Dream Lab possible?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIGjw8YzSH_UAUmMq7WLV0krCNSeQgLJ3AAolc0INa2cnnWnd-44f_54GsqYSAj1DhKjLXb1JpmsN__A011C534319ROIKMdlx0tk60lIeG6d_JpnRs0K-e_2zbJu9Qlk3KRVkeyBv3PJEOpgolaRW236qPDqDsWLzaallJojskPW19p9g2AlOfhK0iGlWbb7kvL351_0BuueyjDMfxN7voo8qXTTPPxNEEF-RG54HpJWt-54yteofEJ06zfh6oD8WanSlnql3v7T8Zb2XUWBjOv40JLnhcFayY-hskJKNpoZ2tdsdhpEG7YZE3tHEkzuNXxYn_mV1tVJPqUV4UukI9T7lZ25Uxnl3NccF3gJ0LSHBlWqWEMglDUu-WRcWkOQEyqUBJ9EFkHibkhVK--wSqzQVG8NnKs0cbxtnb4xxBU/4sk/3qZjVXq2R6ankujT6tliEw/h0/h001.P5R740qJ6s2-bkQ5FNzjzFseEoryZFK30ToDMsUdXfk)** Here's what they've already dug into:
* **The herstory of our movement.** Participants traced over 150 years of immigrant organizing — from the immigrant youth who refused to be ignored and made DACA happen, to the coalitions that have carried this movement forward across generations.

* **The moment we're in.** They named the attacks on our communities honestly and connected them to the pattern our movement has always faced. Whenever we have faced moments of intense fear and uncertainty, we come together so that this country moves toward progress.

* **What comes next.** Over the coming weeks: storytelling and public narrative, event planning, budgeting, artivism, data safety, facilitation, and recruitment — every skill an organizer needs to bring their community together.

Peter, the billionaire class is betting on division and distraction. Participants traced over 150 years of immigrant organizing — from the immigrant youth who refused to be ignored and made DACA happen, to the coalitions that have carried this movement forward across generations. The moment we're in. They named the attacks on our communities honestly and connected them to the pattern our movement has always faced. Whenever we have faced moments of intense fear and uncertainty, we come together so that this country moves toward progress. What comes next. As a journalist, a business owner, a nonprofit leader, and now Jefferson County Commissioner, I've been very fortunate to dedicate my professional life to what I love: serving others.
I've worn a lot of hats as County Commissioner, and I'm especially proud of the investments we've made in JeffCo's wildfire resiliency, substance use disorder treatment programs, and infrastructure. I've also devoted my time to housing affordability — like Phil, I believe folks like our teachers, nurses, and firefighters should be able to live near where they work.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. My opponent doesn't call herself a socialist. She doesn't have to. body:
We can't be in cahoots with the same money that is oppressing us.
#
Pundits want to dismiss this idea as naive, but I want to tell you something.
The last time Democrats in the House won our largest majority since Watergate — in 2018 — 185 Democratic candidates of all backgrounds, rural and urban, progressive and moderate, **ran by not taking a dime in corporate money.**
It's not naive. It's how we win. And it's not just how you win a primary. It's how you win a general election. We can't be in cahoots with the same money that is oppressing us.
It’s not naive. It's what we need, and it most importantly is what you deserve.

name: Tom Fitton
subject: Your Mid-Year Is Critical
body:
Thanks to our generous members, 2026 has already been one of the most impactful years in Judicial Watch history.
| [ ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=14409&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8b1ea2406c2235a7e72abe41770202fd3fe922e3a9843b295763736d5e3f2fd4)
---
Dear Fellow American, Thanks to our generous members, 2026 has _already_ been one of the most impactful years in Judicial Watch history. **_Fighting Race-Based Reparations_**
The Justice Department just filed a motion in our federal lawsuit against Evanston, Illinois' unconstitutional scheme to**give $25,000 taxpayer-funded payments to ONLY black residents -- **_a huge vote of confidence in our case._ **_Cleaning Up Dirty Voter Rolls_**
Our huge Freedom of Information Act lawsuit against California is underway, aiming to force cleanup of over 873,000 dirty, inactive names off their voter rolls and protect fair elections. **_Exposing the Deep State_**
And we are waist-deep in multiple high-level investigations to hold corrupt Deep State actors accountable for their lawfare and persecutions against conservatives, including President Trump. These are just a few examples of hundreds of cases we are fighting FOR YOU. Our investigators _regularly_ **uncover documents** corrupt politicians and Deep State bureaucrats don't want the American people to see. Our lawyers have successfully **_sued many states to clean their voter rolls_** , turning back left-wing schemes to corrupt elections. **And NONE of these investigations, lawsuits, or court victories so far this year would be possible without the support of Judicial Watch donors.** _Not one._ **My Request for You** I trust that, like me, you would like to file **EVEN MORE lawsuits** like these this year to fight for honest elections, expose Deep State secrets, and hold corrupt officials accountable. **That 's why I want to ask you to contribute to this work today by making a gift to our _[Mid-Year Program Drive_](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7).** | [SUPPORT OUR MID YEAR PROGRAM DRIVE ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
This is a mid-year effort to ask Americans like you -- who support Judicial Watch's work and want to help us accomplish even more the rest of the year -- __to make a tax-deductible gift for the very first time._ _ **Is that you today?** Your support for our Mid-Year Program Drive will help Judicial Watch:
* File **_more_** federal lawsuits against **_even more_** states for _honest elections_
* Challenge **_more_** unconstitutional woke programs
* Hold **_even more_** government officials _accountable_ for lawfare against conservatives

**Quite frankly, we can 't do enough to fight for the rule of law.** Our Mid-Year Program Drive must raise at least **_$3.3 million by the end of August_** to sustain and _expand_ our docket and achieve **_more wins_** against corrupt politicians, radical leftists, and Deep State elites. _[Will you make your first-time gift today to help us meet this goal_](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)? | [REFUEL AND EXPAND OUR LAWSUITS - CONTRIBUTE NOW ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)
Your gift truly matters because it will help _refuel_ our programs and ensure our current _investigations_ , _lawsuits_ , and _education_ initiatives stay on track as we pursue **_even more_ _victories for honest government and the rule of law_.** Thank you for considering a gift to our _[Mid-Year Program Drive](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ today so we can fight even more cases to defend the rule of law in the remainder of 2026. Sincerely, Tom Fitton
President Judicial Watch P.S. None of Judicial Watch's many investigations, lawsuits, or court victories in the first half of this year would have happened without the support of generous donors.**Now we want to earn _even more_ wins in the second half of this year**. _[Please make a tax-deductible gift to our Mid-Year Program Drive today](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)_ to help us meet our goal of raising **$3.3 million** more by August 31st. | [MAKE MY MID-YEAR GIFT ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84315&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3e1e7ef2452949c706dc7caa9762525e05a0aa8699a2c23c9aad241394212ee7)

Join us this weekend for our 100 Days Out Weekend of Action to call voters or knock on doors and be part of the team fighting forward for a better future!

name: Sarah McBride
subject: What I said on the Capitol steps
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
I didn’t have the courage to come out until I was 21.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3589%2E21716%2EeSvB7d)
I want to share what I said on the Capitol steps a while back:
I didn’t have the courage to come out until I was 21.
The truth is, I had known who I was for my entire life, and that meant 21 years of pain. 21 years of a kind of homesickness that only went away when I was finally able to get the care I needed.
My biggest regret in life is that I never had a childhood without that pain.
So many years later, I marvel at the courage of transgender young people today, who are sharing themselves with their families and this world despite the toxicity and the hate that too often comes from Congress and from the politicians inside it.
All any of us want is to live a life of purpose and happiness and wholeness, and I carry that with me every day in Congress — especially right now.
**Because Mike Johnson and House Republicans have passed extreme anti-trans bills, including one that risks jailing parents and doctors for affirming transgender children and following medical best practices.**
Republican politicians have made their priorities painfully clear: all they care about is making the rich richer and attacking trans people.
As the only openly trans member of Congress, I refuse to stay silent. I will keep fighting for the dignity, humanity, and fair treatment of every person in Delaware and across the country.
**But if we’re going to tackle this Republican obsession, I need you standing with me.**
[**Rush a donation to help me keep pushing back. Every donation sends a powerful message that we won’t let Republicans get away with weaponizing trans kids as political pawns.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260723-1.g1O8co&refcode=em20260723-3589&amount=5&t=2&akid=3589%2E21716%2EeSvB7d)

clean_body: I didn’t have the courage to come out until I was 21. I want to share what I said on the Capitol steps a while back: I didn’t have the courage to come out until I was 21. The truth is, I had known who I was for my entire life, and that meant 21 years of pain. 21 years of a kind of homesickness that only went away when I was finally able to get the care I needed. My biggest regret in life is that I never had a childhood without that pain. So many years later, I marvel at the courage of transgender young people today, who are sharing themselves with their families and this world despite the toxicity and the hate that too often comes from Congress and from the politicians inside it. All any of us want is to live a life of purpose and happiness and wholeness, and I carry that with me every day in Congress — especially right now. Because Mike Johnson and House Republicans have passed extreme anti-trans bills, including one that risks jailing parents and doctors for affirming transgender children and following medical best practices. Republican politicians have made their priorities painfully clear: all they care about is making the rich richer and attacking trans people. As the only openly trans member of Congress, I refuse to stay silent. I will keep fighting for the dignity, humanity, and fair treatment of every person in Delaware and across the country. But if we’re going to tackle this Republican obsession, I need you standing with me. Thank you, —Sarah

body:

Hi, Peter.
Pete Buttigieg here.
I'm proud to endorse Tom Perriello for Congress in Virginia's 5th District, and I want to tell you why.
Before I do, I should mention that Tom doesn't take a dime from corporate PACs or federal lobbyists. He's building this campaign the same way he's approached public service his entire career: answering to people, not corporate interests.
If you're already with us, please consider making a contribution to help send Tom back to Congress: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em]
One thing I've learned to look for in leaders and candidates is evidence that they will do the right thing when it’s hardest.
Tom has passed that test time and again.
When he served in Congress before, he cast a crucial vote for the Affordable Care Act, knowing it was the right thing to do but that it would cost him politically. He helped expand health care coverage to hundreds of thousands of Virginians. He stood with communities fighting to protect their land and water. And throughout his career, he has shown a willingness to put the public interest ahead of personal or political convenience.
Americans are tired of a politics that seems increasingly disconnected from their everyday lives. People want leaders focused on lowering costs, expanding opportunity, protecting fundamental freedoms, and making government work better for the people it serves.
Those goals can be unifying, not divisive. Yet Washington has become a place where displaying common sense requires uncommon courage and strength.
What we need now is the right kind of leaders in Congress who can make that body start to reflect what Americans actually want and need.
Tom understands that. He has spent his career bringing people together around solutions that improve people's lives, and I know he'll bring that same sense of purpose back to Congress.
This race matters. Virginia's 5th District is one of the seats that could determine whether Democrats win back the House majority. Tom has already proven once before that this district is winnable – he remains the only Democrat to flip this seat in a generation.
But winning it again will take all of us.
Will you join me in supporting Tom Perriello today? Any contribution you can make will help him build the campaign needed to win this race and help secure a House majority that can move the country forward. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/perriello-em?amount=50]

Peter, I apologize for the raw honesty, but I have been speaking with the top brass, and the prognosis isn't good. The liberals know this is the _most_ important Senate race in the country, and they are pouring in a tsunami of outside money to block President Trump’s agenda. Honestly, I’m distraught. body:
# THE AARON DAY SHOW
Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy
S3E22 • Jul 23
## S3E22: You Don't Own Your Stocks. EXPOSED.
[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/tAkh5qBp8X6?e=938a87a89b&c2id=c1b996ddd6cdaaf4cddb384f099ac837)
You don't own your stocks.
Read that again.
That share of Apple, Tesla, or your index fund? You don't hold it. A custodian does. And under the CLARITY and GENIUS Act frameworks, every equity, bond, and real-world asset is being marched onto programmable, surveilled rails.
Tokenized. Traceable. Freezable. Revokable.
They call it modernization. It's the final phase of Own Nothing. When your stocks live on a permissioned ledger, a bureaucrat with a keyboard can flip a switch and your retirement is gone. No court. No appeal. Just a compliance flag on a token you never actually owned.
Tonight I'm going solo and taking a hammer to the illusion. I'll show you exactly how the tokenization pipeline works, who benefits, and why every asset class is next. Real estate. Treasuries. Your 401k. All of it moving onto rails they control.
Then we talk exit.
Zano is private money AND private tokenized assets. Not KYC'd. Not surveilled. Not programmable by them. It's the parallel system being built while you still have time to move.
And exit at the ballot too. My Senate run is a direct vote against the technocracy grid these bills are cementing into law. Silence is consent. Show up.
Tune in tonight. Bring a friend who still thinks their brokerage account is theirs.
Join me live tonight and learn how to actually own what's yours.

Friend, The Deepwater Horizon disaster in 2010 taught us a hard lesson about what can happen when safety oversight fails. Eleven workers lost their lives, and millions of barrels of oil flooded the Gulf. Now the Trump administration is proposing to combine two offshore agencies into a single Marine Minerals Administration **while shrinking Interior’s workforce and pushing to open more ocean areas to drilling and seabed mining.** Fewer experienced experts overseeing more complex projects raises real risks for workers, coastal communities, marine life, and taxpayers. **The safeguards put in place after Deepwater Horizon are critical.**_We can’t let the agencies that promote offshore development and enforce safety rules become intertwined._ **That’s why I’ve joined colleagues in Congress to call on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to investigate this proposal.** We need to know whether Interior has a clear plan, the right staff and scientific expertise, and the safeguards needed to keep safety and environmental reviews independent from industry pressure. What happens on the coasts doesn’t stay on the coasts. Weak federal oversight sets a dangerous precedent that can hurt Tribal nations, Western watersheds, and the public lands and waters New Mexicans depend on. We need strong, independent reviews so communities across the country are protected. [_**Will you add your name supporting our demand for a full, independent GAO investigation before this merger moves forward? Together, we can tell Congress: we won’t risk another Deepwater Horizon by tearing down the protections designed to prevent it.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135865503/635576103/-1172592465?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260723_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZGYyNjVkMi1jODg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wkwzNxdJ44F2I3Q1xtVx16dOD1_tr8oV0cgO1AzmUYA=&emci=93f265d2-c886-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=adf265d2-c886-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=252045) | [SIGN THE PETITION](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135865504/635576104/-1172592465?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20260723_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZGYyNjVkMi1jODg2LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wkwzNxdJ44F2I3Q1xtVx16dOD1_tr8oV0cgO1AzmUYA=&emci=93f265d2-c886-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=adf265d2-c886-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=252045)

body:
Federal audit questions nearly $54 million in Colorado Medicaid home-care payments
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** A federal audit flagged nearly [$54 million in undocumented Colorado Medicaid home-care billing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) — the second Medicaid program flagged this year. A State Department [report on Cuban subversion names a Denver DSA member](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) among 40 socialists who visited Cuba last October, and DSA nominee Melat Kiros called for [electing more immigrants](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to counter America's "exploitative" global role. Elsewhere, luxury car owners are using Montana LLCs to [dodge registration fees](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), a judge dismissed a Mesa County sheriff's [ICE cooperation lawsuit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), analysts warned of a [looming power shortfall](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as Xcel retires dispatchable generation, and [Children's Hospital pleaded not guilty](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to violating a court order on gender-affirming prescriptions.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** New Jersey Gov. Sherrill acknowledged about [6,600 self-identified noncitizens were mistakenly registered to vote](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) due to a software error — days after DHS alleged the state could have up to 35,152 noncitizens on its rolls.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Cory Gaines questions whether the Golden Range housing project's state land deals and tax financing amount to [picking winners at taxpayer expense](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Colleen Enos warns pro-regulation groups are pushing model legislation, after wins in Connecticut and New Jersey, that could [impose registry requirements on Colorado homeschoolers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And Dr. Brian Joondeph argues Flock cameras have proven valuable but [need stronger audit safeguards](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) against misuse.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, July 23, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Federal audit questions nearly $54 million in Colorado Medicaid home-care payments](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado can’t fully document millions of dollars it billed for Medicaid home care. That’s the finding of a new federal audit.
The Office of Inspector General wants Colorado to return $8.07 million in federal money it says the state was not entitled to claim for personal care in a single budget year, the one ending June 30, 2024. Auditors questioned another $45.69 million and told the state to work it out with CMS.
The $8.07 million is a recommended refund. The $45.69 million is a different story. It’s still under review, and CMS could recover all of it, some of it or none. Either way, nobody has ordered Colorado to repay the full $53.8 million.
In the sample, auditors kept hitting records that didn’t add up. Where the care happened. How long it ran. Who showed up to provide it. Whether the bill matched the services and rates Colorado had approved.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Denver DSA member joined Cuba delegation now mentioned in State Department report](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A State Department report tying DSA's Cuba trips to a Denver chapter member raises fresh questions about the group's ties to the Castro regime._
* **A Denver connection to Havana:** One of the 40 Democratic Socialists of America members who flew to Cuba last October — delivering aid and touring Cuban institutions — came from Denver, and the local chapter later held a public "reportback" event on the trip.
* **State Department names names:** A new 100-page State Department report, "Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism," dedicates a full section to DSA, noting the delegation was hosted by ICAP, a Castro-founded organization the Treasury Department sanctioned this June as an arm of the Cuban government.
* **Alignment, not infiltration, the report argues:** The document stops short of calling DSA a Cuban front, instead concluding the group "freely embraced" Cuba's worldview on its own — while DSA itself openly confirms the trips, its Venceremos Fund, and its 2019 vote to join a pro-Cuba coalition that includes the Communist Party USA.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

NOTE: I am not a Trump fanboy nor a partisan ideologue; I am a conservative who values the truth. You may dislike or disagree with Mr. Trump or certain members of his cabinet, or some of the 56 items on this list (sourced from Jeff Childers in his Coffee &Covid blog) but it provides hard details for your consideration._ __
**[The Hidden Trust Weapon: Olly, Olly, Oxen Free!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JULY 19** _“Olly, olly, oxen free!” If you’re smiling right now, you’re probably remembering the same thing I am. Long before smartphones, video games, and streaming television, neighborhood kids had an amazing ability to entertain themselves. We’d ride our bikes until the streetlights came on, play baseball in empty lots, build forts out of scrap lumber, and, when the evening shadows grew just a little longer, someone would shout, “Let’s play hide-and-seek!”_**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** __

name: Adam Schwarze - Former Navy SEAL
subject: The next fraud scandal in MN
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Schwarze for Senate
body:
It's time to solve the Walz-Flanagan fraud in Minnesota once and for all. |
---

I am mad, Fellow Conservative.

I've fought my entire life for the United States of America. I fought for democracy all over the world.

And to learn that someone might have voted **_USING MY NAME_** while I was 2,000 miles away in SEAL training! This is a threat to our democracy.

How can I be in two places at once? _**The answer is another fraud scandal. This time, rampant voter fraud.**_

We can thank Governor Tim Walz and his "co-governor" Peggy Flanagan.

[](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=dfa46834018345cf9b03cddc477b3fae&_e=D9bHaVHXCC4ubzNRi_zzJzI9PSPyr7OWF9CrsFUC2ZDEf-XJ4WqFsqgLm1Takj64hJSHHw-msq69jj1VEZKdbAWOOY1OwOFInKp97pv8tL45TN--tu57RYo1XMRPQD4U2wthHj71StPCwnzzpScU6oPaDsZPJZjMk8zClueuoB32yACefEtQD7rg8XrPgjuJJSqC0Y6ktxFXxm-VxqYr_WPzS0BqdC-P-kgB5hq4_a2AabnDmhA-EBPNbTRD-sA9IZqRCYnstgQPff3z8T4Xx_ku1_VmIqRTRxzcUVy7Rimaa7nfqpn_mYEjhsaPD2nf8WMa4wAdXIQYUAwkJZLCHPsV3TqyDAXt2e1Q19NKTVC6w7h7ya1REKTArqmfpIsdHcsJ9vWoMmjp4F3TO_tn51l70MQ9jTazTdGAhk9Hl7pCld6d5rMPOOtKMijlbqUBm5JS9rrSCyfAstlpqbXnlXn8qgai9PeROU6gzEfGycvQLxiSz1-Bs4Lyx6apfcX1uxDFM0e3f0jV4sq0fptC9MDAeQ4LyEPj7SNaW_stgwpqVnDzQSAcV23vGdvUQWNaZzOvcJPBdGrODrjv_KeqIHVEo0h7uXLAzK1QwxbA__PzTNM4b107OxIKFbMzahkNRXiBr1P57qu7Sd-DEgsrinJJJII814ea0CQqavSk3BBo2yqfCa8XWSSO7jCUpYXixt8pqjU0vD8ylvgH4mvBsXXkzzFhGopKbpnXFwT3BfgnOer9bNZCT9kqpJYcFZRl_PU1stU0jbWIeYKDz9mGkC7N1xfSKzAK_k0jUWqD6f2g7esm3gFWZZNi_f9AOGjC9_oRkEkRAs2LWJBlNDb1OA%3D%3D)
This clearly shows that we have an election integrity issue in our state.

One of the pillars and foundational principles of democracy is free, fair, and transparent elections, and we don't have any of those things right now in the United States of America.

_**It’s time to solve the problem.**_

| | **_Meet Rob:_** Born and raised in Kingston, PA, Rob Bresnahan is currently serving his first term as PA-08’s homegrown Congressman. He’s a fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, and the only representative in Congress who is part of the National Electrical Contractors Association. A product of the American Dream, Rob learned the true meaning of hard work by getting his hands dirty early and often. He wired junction boxes, ran heavy equipment, drove trucks, and learned the value of an honest day’s work in the process. His family instilled the values of hard work, discipline, and perseverance in him at a young age – and Rob has stayed true to these foundational values all his life. At just 19 years old, Rob joined his family’s business as the CFO for Kuharchik Construction. He became the CEO of the company in 2013. Rob spent over a decade working and connecting with blue-collar Americans across the country before running for Congress in 2024. He was outspent 2:1 in his race against a 12-year Democrat that year, but the people of Northeastern Pennsylvania demanded change when they sent Rob to be their fighter in Washington. Through his experience as an electrical contractor, Rob saw the real world struggles facing America’s blue-collar workers first hand. Wages are not keeping up with the skyrocketing cost of living, and Americans who wake up every day and pay their dues are being left out to dry by their elected officials. But Rob’s voting record in Congress tells a different story. He’s stood up for hardworking Americans at every opportunity, regardless of partisan politics. Simply put, Rob Bresnahan brings both insight and candid concern for blue-collar America to Congress that your run-of-the-mill representatives don’t. Every day that he steps foot on Capitol Hill, Rob is 100% devoted to restoring America’s energy independence, deregulating the economy, and bringing well-paying jobs back to the great commonwealth of Pennsylvania. While he’s still serving his freshman term in Congress, Rob has already introduced key legislation to re-invest in American trades and pave avenues to success for young people who forgo a traditional college education. Now running for re-election in one of the most pivotal battleground races in the country, Rob is stepping up to the plate once again to deliver for the people of PA-08 and preserve our Republican House majority for the remainder of President Trump’s second term.
