body:
Peter,

Let's be honest about what Donald Trump has done to this country.

He has weaponized the government against its own people, hollowed out our institutions, enabled ICE to brutalize our communities, and stripped our country for parts to be sold to the highest bidder in order to enrich himself. Perhaps worst of all, he has made cruelty his policy.

The costs of all of this are real — we see them in rising prices, in the loss of our civil liberties, and in the fear that too many Americans are living with on a daily basis.

But here's what Mary Trump has always known about Donald: he counts on us being so demoralized by the chaos he unleashes that we will give up.
He couldn’t be more wrong.

Because today, Mary is launching Transcend PAC, a team dedicated to electing bold leaders who have the courage to restore accountability, protect our institutions, and transcend this dark era in our country’s history.

Transcend PAC endorses and directly contributes to candidates who offer a transformative vision for America’s future, including: government accountability; taxing billionaires; regulating big tech; advocating for real climate solutions; strengthening our civil rights protections; reforming our institutions; increasing wages; and rebuilding and fortifying our education, healthcare, housing, and infrastructure.

This is the solution to everything Donald and a complicit Republican Party have done: Organized action to support candidates and causes that pledge to do the work that will lead to real, substantive change. Peter,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I am ready to continue his legacy. | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. **I am calling on Greg Abbott to sign an emergency executive order to put a moratorium on data centers until the Legislature meets to give Texans a seat at the table.** After years of Greg Abbott opening the floodgates to his data center donors, we need to put a stop to the madness until we can thoughtfully regulate this fast-changing industry.
This past weekend I visited the site of Project Matador, which will be the largest data center in the world, right outside of Amarillo. I walked the five miles of the future site and met with members of the community to truly understand the impact of this data center going up in their backyard. Watch the walk here:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/407f013e-212f-4417-b245-ebedce99455d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The richest men in the world are running up your electric bill, and you can thank Greg Abbott for that. He's sold our land and drinking water to the highest bidder, all while we foot the bill. Abbott has created the Wild Wild West for data centers where, at every turn, corporate donors get exactly what they want, and everyday Texans get nothing.
Abbott signed one of the country's biggest data center giveaways, promised to make Texas the "epicenter" of AI data centers, and then took millions from the companies and executives cashing in. **Under his leadership, Texas is fast-tracking approvals for major data centers that are now on target to use enough energy to power 28 million homes for a year by 2028.**
**The Governor has the sole power to stop this madness TODAY.** He can call an emergency special session to ensure basic protections are in place for the people of Texas, including:
## **1\. American Union Jobs:**
Data center operators in the state should hire skilled, licensed, union Texan workers at a livable wage. Texans don't just deserve a seat at the table; they deserve a piece of the pie.
## **2\. Texans Deserve a Seat at the Table:**
Communities should decide if and how data centers are built in their area. Until we bring the people of Texas to the table, we must immediately pause the building of data centers until the Legislature grants communities the power to vote on or negotiate with data centers.
## **3\. Lower Costs for Texans:**
A handful of billionaires are profiting off the backs of hardworking families. These data centers are owned by some of the richest men in the world -- they should pay for them themselves. The standard for data centers has meant that all of the cost burden falls on us consumers. We are forced to compete for energy and water, all while big business gets a tax break. Data center developers must prove Texas households won't pay more for electricity or water, including the hidden costs passed through for grid upgrades, transmission, and new capacity.
## **4\. Demand Transparency:**
These data center owners need to be up front about the risks of data center construction, how much energy they require, and how much noise they will create -- without hiding behind NDAs. Our communities deserve full transparency.
## **5\. Water and Power for Texans First:**
This one is real simple. Data centers must disclose how much water they intend to use. If a data center threatens a community's water supply, their water contract would become void. Families should not be competing with corporations to have access to clean water.
Texans deserve better than Abbott. Innovation is important, but so is taking care of your people. As the next Governor of Texas, I plan to value both.
-- Gina
**[P.S. If you 're ready to get Abbott out of the Governor's mansion and want to see real change in Texas, can I count on you to chip in $5 or whatever makes sense for you today? It's going to take everyone pitching in to help get us across the finish line.](https://substack.com/redirect/41f9d6b7-dd8f-484a-a362-f7d68dd43285?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

If a data center threatens a community's water supply, their water contract would become void. Families should not be competing with corporations to have access to clean water. Texans deserve better than Abbott. Innovation is important, but so is taking care of your people. As the next Governor of Texas, I plan to value both. -- Gina | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Gina Hinojosa PO Box 300095, Austin, TX 78703 ? ?

Patriot, My mom was a teenager when she found out she was pregnant with me. She chose to have me anyway, and my grandparents stepped in to raise me in the Deep South. If the Left had their way, my story could've ended right then and there... I have some exciting news to share with you.
Dr. Amish Shah just won his Democratic primary in Arizona's 1st Congressional District. And I need you to understand just how important this moment is:
First, let me tell you about Amish.
He's an emergency room physician — a doctor who has spent his career at the bedside of patients on the worst days of their lives. He served in the Arizona State House, where he passed more bills than any other Democrat. He's the son of immigrants. And he's running to bring the values of hard work, opportunity, and common-sense problem-solving to Congress.
But here's what makes this race so critical...
Arizona's 1st District may be the single most contested battleground district in the entire country. This is a seat Republicans have held through seven straight elections — and in 2022, Democrats came within eight-tenths of a single percentage point of flipping it. This year, with the right candidate and the right resources, we can finally win it.
Amish Shah is that candidate. But he cannot do it alone.
The Republican machine and their dark-money allies are going to pour everything they have into holding this seat. They know what's at stake. The path to taking back the House runs directly through districts exactly like this one — and if we want to stop Trump's MAGA agenda, we have to win here.
That's why I'm asking you to step up today.
Will you split a contribution between Amish Shah's general election campaign and Equal Opportunity Now right now? Your support goes directly to flipping one of the most important seats in America and building the movement to elect fighters like Amish all across the country. | | Derek,

Earlier this month, our housing bill, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, officially became the law of the land. Double woohoo!

Donald Trump refused to sign it.

It didn't matter. Since Congress passed it and he took no action, it automatically went into effect while he was snoozing.

But this fight was never about Donald Trump. It was about whether Congress could act to make life more affordable for working families.

And the Democrats delivered a new bipartisan law to lower costs and do just that.

This is the biggest housing law in more than 30 years — a landmark bill that will build more homes, lower housing costs, and help more families achieve the dream of homeownership.

Here’s what happened, Derek. Weeks ago, Republicans and Democrats passed this bill with overwhelming bipartisan support. I’m talking more than 90-percent of lawmakers in Congress voted for this housing affordability bill.

Then Donald Trump decided to play politics.

For 10 days, he threw a tantrum. Refusing to sign the bill because he wanted to use it as leverage to force Congress to pass his voter suppression bill, the SAVE Act.

Trump even dismissed this housing bill as "a yawn."

The good news is that the Constitution doesn't give a president a veto by neglect. If Congress is still in session and a president refuses to act on a bill for 10 days, that bill becomes law anyway.

So, thanks for nothing, Donald.

With the passage of this bill, we’re going to:
* Build more homes by cutting unnecessary red tape and speeding up construction, giving families more affordable places to live.

* Expand homeownership by making it easier for working people to qualify for mortgages and buy their first home.

* Put families ahead of Wall Street by stopping private equity firms from buying up the single-family homes that should belong to people who want to live in them.

This is worth celebrating, but I'm not confusing one victory for the finish line.

There’s a whole lot more we need our government to do to actually address the issues that people are struggling with. The good news is that we just proved we CAN get legislation passed that actually meets the moment. We just need to continue to keep up the fight.

# **NYC landlords sue over Mamdani 's illegal rent freeze**
A coalition of New York City landlords **[has filed a lawsuit](https://substack.com/redirect/72d17385-7c55-49e3-92ad-1f332b0e5a96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** challenging Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze for nearly one million rent-stabilized apartments, represented by attorney Randy Mastro. Mastro argued the Rent Guidelines Board abandoned its legal obligation to independently evaluate economic data and instead delivered a predetermined outcome at the mayor's direction, calling the process "blatantly illegal."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72d17385-7c55-49e3-92ad-1f332b0e5a96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Landlord groups contend the freeze ignores rising operating costs** -- including soaring taxes, utilities, and insurance -- that are straining property owners already operating on thin margins. Mastro pointed to the resignation of longtime board member Alex Armlovich on the morning of the vote as evidence the process lacked integrity, though Armlovich said he left for a new job in philanthropy.
* **Mamdani, elected on a housing affordability platform, defended the freeze** as necessary relief for tenants facing persistent high living costs. The board approved the measure last month in a move critics called a rubber-stamp of his campaign promise.

| | Dear Peter,
Our campaign is gaining momentum! We have now raised $700,000 and Kshama was just interviewed on popular podcasts like the _Katie Halper Show_ and _Jimmy Dore_. **This coming Monday she will be appearing on** _**Breaking Points**_**, which has 2 million subscribers.**
Kshama is fighting to tax the rich to fund free healthcare for all, to end all military aid to Israel, and for a full arms embargo against the Israeli state. Meanwhile, the Democrats and Republicans in Congress, including Kshama’s opponent, Democrat Adam Smith, have been hard at work funding more wars and increasing the power of the genocidal Israeli military. The US House of Representatives just passed a $1.15 trillion war budget with a provision to fuse the US and Israeli militaries. This bill was co-sponsored by Adam Smith, who has voted repeatedly to fund the genocide in Gaza and to block UN food aid from Gaza in the context of mass starvation of Palestinians.
[AIPAC thanked Adam Smith after today's vote](https://us.list-manage.com/1BAnUO38Oow?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15), saying **"AIPAC members deeply appreciate House leadership, House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (R‐AL) and Ranking Member Adam Smith (D‐WA),** and Republican and Democratic champions for advancing the pro-Israel provisions in the bill, which support American jobs, enhance troop safety, and keep the United States at the forefront of defense innovation by leveraging the enduring U.S.-Israel partnership."
We are fighting to defeat AIPAC darling and billionaire-backed Adam Smith and put his 29-year long blood-drenched career where it belongs: in the dustbin of history. This would be a massive victory on its own. However, we can achieve far more than that. **We have a historic opportunity to elect the first ever revolutionary socialist to the US Congress.** But to do this, we need all of you to put as much or your time and energy as you can into these final days of the primary election. We need everyone who wants Kshama to win to go all-out to support this campaign.
There has never been anyone in Congress with a track record like Kshama's. Kshama used her elected position on the Seattle City Council to build militant mass movements and go to war against the political establishment. She never backed away from calling out any politician when they acted against the interests of the working class and oppressed communities. The movements she built forced Democrats to vote again and again for things they had opposed previously, including the highest minimum wage in the nation and the Amazon Tax. That's the kind of political leadership we need in Congress. But we will need to fight hard to get Kshama elected because the Democratic and Republican establishments, along with their many gatekeepers, have used every dirty trick in the book to try to block Kshama from getting into the general election.
**We need you to help us get out the vote, so come out to**[**Volunteer Day on Sunday July 26th at 11AM**](https://us.list-manage.com/xVooCBWtDp3?e=bbdb764b3a&c2id=8b3f9b08d69d5a7a0bcc2cd67f268e15)**.** We will have four simultaneous meetups at different locations around the district. Join us at whichever location works best for you:
* Judkins Park Light Rail Station, East Entrance, Seattle
* Columbia Park, Seattle
* Liberty Park, Renton
* Les Gove Park, Auburn Farmers Market

Come out on Sunday to talk with thousands of working people all around the district! No experience is needed! Our campaign organizers will train everyone on how to volunteer effectively for our campaign. Snacks and water will be provided.
Solidarity,Kshama for Congress

body:

body:
The NDAA should be about defending our country. This does the opposite. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGq4v3lLteMi29U_8-bUhnou--DJFNnviyzHsoDR1_G4pmCnlXidlrmOZZX-qmP-g-tdtmo8Di1LWOxPuTenYnabVDgF5HeDdBkH5w5YWeehQ-IH1D7LyZj5gLyHMYUkn_jUB4dRZmrjag4ukNOM24VolBYu23Bqqb1qjAJj7CEO66iCr2PuckbPXRLXuXpl4p8gh2oWhIlsezFhj-0KYiVqUbrDqKwyBu4tbe9sghhmo/4sk/U2hFONy3Rs6ewUZEjgGoKA/h0/h001.KEIXLGc7xN9MpxXis9JJyKQJ2LMEU85mBoJ2y8cphWM)

Peter, Yesterday, the House narrowly passed the National Defense Authorization Act, or NDAA. Nearly every Democrat voted against it, and nearly every Republican voted for it. My opponent, Keith Self, was one of them.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yn3vU-sJ4-D5Sm8WJzTFwGFvPDuSAfRMkrLp0J-9wzT00JzthQiOaN4Bw4YG5dQSHV0lNOTEsOrYZ1VUJmI6uNeYVNipCT4_dP_iadtOriLf0dTEJJkIaqYNe4Raprvtgyo6cAGd3rn_aqNEoaJCC1eNGjLDhwREtTMaXGD0PbsSBWy9jWQR4nejYG3Kh7RMm0OT0uZZ2msk9pBbx1jSpz45UOiSTLekhq__nFZvR8iiHfhSadW3JZvE2JXGGciOHT0LYftfJM8chIM7sLpjsdxocQbH_t9_bzSzQ0qwou5bzH7Ks2jh4NHP6eh1ijARi8XVvnPq8Oa7jFcUqwTC-a7jqMYorfnJ_zjZqbmVX4JufwQZ6TgY9mqTotQ736vvg/4sk/U2hFONy3Rs6ewUZEjgGoKA/h1/h001.7WcNgcfZXt2D6438xbpTRQ9E58ZC3vpysCa5YyHJtkU)

I served in the United States Air Force for 20 years, and have continued to work in the Defense industry after my time in service. I’ve seen countless Defense budgets pass Congress and counted on those resources to do my job.
I know how important the NDAA is, and why it has to be non-partisan. But the bill that passed the House this week was not only deeply partisan – it contains a dangerous provision that I could not and would not have supported if I were in Congress today.
Section 219, a provision buried deep in an otherwise standard Defense appropriations bill, intertwines America’s defense industrial base with Israel in an unprecedented way.
It expands – even mandates – cooperation on research, development, testing, advanced technologies, missile defense, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and defense manufacturing.
This is some of our most sensitive military technology, and if this bill passes the Senate and becomes law, it will codify a requirement to share that technology with Israeli Defense Forces – no matter how they might use it.
[That’s an unacceptable abdication of our responsibility to be good stewards of this technology and protect American interests. Help me flip this seat and send me to Congress to stop this dangerous precedent.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yn3vU-sJ4-D5Sm8WJzTFwErIuXta_wpMOWSa8YM_F5VEkaw8u-UU9-VU6p_jCSjFhJTtRBFX3H1PUFF9OR9Ut4ZpbnUDHkVnHcsVx7YANeNpXX-ao3cV6zYaSJ-qyAcfoxZnz9pJxQe0lqaobBNUBzk-b8Q2DNiLgPlOZYq4tLo5GzZqtWIhjIMjh8qSAlaEzm9mZOsXzyDlfl3x6WTM3LVYKLkFW1UCb2iJ7SCSWt8qg5gQef_L6_Y5g2dofTElJwykvwktN1KvRnQVuNJbKwLzz_MMV0hLec1xi50YR14HvZG9r8C3QbNFA_rbW6lBm-eWcPnPViCi1EzpqIc7y8y1wZKzFXRNpSmBomHdixb6lbwCzoJgDFCCu4yJyFMPg/4sk/U2hFONy3Rs6ewUZEjgGoKA/h2/h001.dYik6PJ-DLDyCKsyJ_vIpLcwj0Wu5Igk8Ni5wpOHKL4)
I support every ally’s right to defend itself. In fact, if we stop selling American-made defensive systems to our allies, we’ll quickly drive them into the arms of competitors like China and Russia. Strong alliances are in America’s national interest.
But there is a fundamental difference between selling American defense systems to our allies and sending highly sensitive taxpayer-funded research and development dollars overseas.
American taxpayer dollars should build American technology, create American jobs, strengthen American manufacturing, and preserve America’s defense industrial advantage.
Major decisions that deepen our military commitments abroad or intertwine our defense industry with another nation’s should be debated openly and voted on individually, not quietly folded into must-pass legislation.
[That’s the transparency and representative leadership you deserve, and it’s what I will fight for in Congress.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yn3vU-sJ4-D5Sm8WJzTFwE6uw9ZOwtN2PSLwOeTdKVPlUShp0CPtApoFkpC_QzEd0tnGdgAjCu-eCkYSwsoNHw-W_H3VccNzIV3-oJIVPYsxjqgC37jKT7upIU-3ZjKOX3ZhiP33Wy2riPfdroRbf9NnLJx0TM3tKLOEurKEzRSiYA9C9KF5JilrhGw6fzdYxezD3vXHLiQbhLcb3DgdO7C5LRAZ_P2MPO_wES4RS8FIsrJwSepDUiMqKHjuH4kgfWYaonrFy2yAnOuaUdIkPulpkbwKgArHnP3PsY9jeq-VwVjE-GqeQ7N91fpMHyLP_Z53OY5LWoxpbxjrmwnhb6AALROF2PoQ-fkkZ0PxB7hbFIWhlpQhNkkfkN2dll6sQ/4sk/U2hFONy3Rs6ewUZEjgGoKA/h3/h001.9gBJM-TLndWKgsirXvW__0yn1-sHW8xi17jKq-L6Xfw)

This week he also voted for the House budget resolution to authorize another $73 billion to continue Trump’s war with Iran – after rejecting the War Powers resolution that would have forced the president to abide by our constitution and earn the support of Congress for continuing that conflict.
Just another blank check for a Middle East war with no end in sight.
He also voted for H.R. 8595, handing another $2.1 billion in assistance to Jordan, including direct support for its government and military financing.
Families right here in CD3 are struggling to put food on the table, keep a roof over their heads, or pay for basic healthcare while our tax dollars are being shipped abroad to blow up schools and hospitals.
If there was ever any doubt, there shouldn’t be anymore.
Keith Self, and the Trump administration he supports, are not America First. They aren’t fiscally responsible. They aren’t morally accountable.
They must be removed from power before they can do more harm.

clean_body: The NDAA should be about defending our country. This does the opposite. | | Peter, Yesterday, the House narrowly passed the National Defense Authorization Act, or NDAA. Nearly every Democrat voted against it, and nearly every Republican voted for it. My opponent, Keith Self, was one of them. | I served in the United States Air Force for 20 years, and have continued to work in the Defense industry after my time in service. I’ve seen countless Defense budgets pass Congress and counted on those resources to do my job. I know how important the NDAA is, and why it has to be non-partisan. But the bill that passed the House this week was not only deeply partisan – it contains a dangerous provision that I could not and would not have supported if I were in Congress today. Section 219, a provision buried deep in an otherwise standard Defense appropriations bill, intertwines America’s defense industrial base with Israel in an unprecedented way. It expands – even mandates – cooperation on research, development, testing, advanced technologies, missile defense, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and defense manufacturing. This is some of our most sensitive military technology, and if this bill passes the Senate and becomes law, it will codify a requirement to share that technology with Israeli Defense Forces – no matter how they might use it. I support every ally’s right to defend itself. In fact, if we stop selling American-made defensive systems to our allies, we’ll quickly drive them into the arms of competitors like China and Russia. Strong alliances are in America’s national interest. But there is a fundamental difference between selling American defense systems to our allies and sending highly sensitive taxpayer-funded research and development dollars overseas. American taxpayer dollars should build American technology, create American jobs, strengthen American manufacturing, and preserve America’s defense industrial advantage. Major decisions that deepen our military commitments abroad or intertwine our defense industry with another nation’s should be debated openly and voted on individually, not quietly folded into must-pass legislation. This was just the latest in a spate of reckless votes from my opponent. This week he also voted for the House budget resolution to authorize another $73 billion to continue Trump’s war with Iran – after rejecting the War Powers resolution that would have forced the president to abide by our constitution and earn the support of Congress for continuing that conflict. Just another blank check for a Middle East war with no end in sight. He also voted for H.R. 8595, handing another $2.1 billion in assistance to Jordan, including direct support for its government and military financing. Families right here in CD3 are struggling to put food on the table, keep a roof over their heads, or pay for basic healthcare while our tax dollars are being shipped abroad to blow up schools and hospitals. If there was ever any doubt, there shouldn’t be anymore. Keith Self, and the Trump administration he supports, are not America First. They aren’t fiscally responsible. They aren’t morally accountable. They must be removed from power before they can do more harm.
